قَالَ مُوسَى: (( وَأَهِلِّي بِالْحَجِّ )). وَقَالَ سُلَيْمَانُ: (( وَاصْنَعِي مَا يَصْنَعُ الْمُسْلِمُونَ فِي حَجِّهِمْ )).

فَلَمَّا كَانَ لَيْلَةُ الصَّدَرِ أَمَرَ - يَعْنِي رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ - عَبْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ، فَذَهَبَ بِهَا إِلَى التَّنْعِيمِ. زَادَ مُوسَى: (( فَأَهَلَّتْ بِعُمْرَةٍ مَكَانَ عُمْرَتِهَا، وَطَافَتْ بِالْبَيْتِ، فَقَضَى اللَّهُ عُمْرَتَهَا وَحَجَّهَا )).

صحيح: رواه أبو داود (١٧٧٨)، والنسائيّ (٢٧١٧)، وابن خزيمة (٢٦٠٤)، وابن حبان (٣٧٩٢).

4911 — ‘A’ishah said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ near the sighting of the crescent of Dhu al-Hijjah. When he reached Dhul-Hulayfah, he said: “Whoever wishes to enter ihram for Hajj, let him do so; and whoever wishes to enter ihram for Umrah, let him do so for Umrah.”

Musa said in the narration of Wuhaib: “As for me, had I not brought sacrificial animals, I would have entered ihram for Umrah.” And in the narration of Hammad ibn Salamah: “But as for me, I am entering ihram for Hajj, for I have the sacrificial animals with me.”

Then they agreed on the wording: “So I was among those who entered ihram for Umrah. Then on the way I menstruated. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to me while I was crying, and he said: ‘What makes you cry?’ I said: I wish I had not gone out this year. He said: ‘Set aside your Umrah, undo your hair, and comb it.’”

Musa said: “And enter ihram for Hajj.” Sulayman said: “And do what the Muslims do in their Hajj.”

Then when the night of departure came, he — meaning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ — ordered ‘Abd al-Rahman, and he took her to al-Tan‘im. Musa added: “So she entered ihram for an Umrah in place of her earlier Umrah, and she circumambulated the House, and Allah completed her Umrah and her Hajj.”

Authentic: narrated by Abu Dawud (1778), al-Nasa’i (2717), Ibn Khuzaymah (2604), and Ibn Hibban (3792).

٤٩١٣ — عن أم المؤمنين عائشة، قالت: خَرَجْنَا مَعَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ وَلا نُرَى إِلَّا أَنَّهُ الْحَجُّ، فَلَمَّا قَدِمْنَا تَطَوَّفْنَا بِالْبَيْتِ، أَمَرَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ مَنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ سَاقَ الْهَدْيَ أَنْ يَحِلَّ، فَحَلَّ مَنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ سَاقَ الْهَدْيَ، وَنِسَاؤُهُ لَمْ يَسُقْنَ، فَأَحْلَلْنَ.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاريّ (١٥٦١)، ومسلم (١٢٨ :١٢١١).

وفي رواية عند مسلم (١٣٠)، عن عائشة، قالت: قَدِمَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ لِأَرْبَعٍ مَضَيْنَ مِنْ ذِي الْحِجَّةِ أَوْ خَمْسٍ، فَدَخَلَ عَلَيَّ وَهُوَ غَضْبَانُ، فَقُلْتُ: مَنْ أَغْضَبَكَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ؟ أَدْخَلَهُ اللَّهُ النَّارَ. قَالَ: (( أَوَمَا شَعَرْتِ أَنِّي أَمَرْتُ النَّاسَ بِأَمْرٍ، فَإِذَا هُمْ يَتَرَدَّدُونَ؟ )) قَالَ الْحَكَمُ: كَأَنَّهُمْ يَتَرَدَّدُونَ. أَحْسِبُ. (( وَلَوْ أَنِّي اسْتَقْبَلْتُ مِنْ أَمْرِي مَا اسْتَدْبَرْتُ، مَا سُقْتُ الْهَدْيَ مَعِي حَتَّى أَشْتَرِيَهُ، ثُمَّ أَحِلُّ كَمَا حَلُّوا )).

4913 — The Mother of the Believers, ‘A’ishah, said: We went out with the Prophet ﷺ not thinking it was anything but Hajj. Then when we arrived, we circled the House. The Prophet ﷺ ordered whoever had not brought sacrificial animals to come out of ihram, so those who had not brought sacrificial animals came out of ihram. And his wives had not brought sacrificial animals, so they too came out of ihram.

Agreed upon: narrated by al-Bukhari (1561) and Muslim (1211/128).

And in a narration in Muslim (130), from ‘A’ishah, she said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived on the fourth or fifth of Dhu al-Hijjah, and he entered upon me while angry. So I said: Who angered you, O Messenger of Allah ﷺ? May Allah enter him into the Fire. He said: “Have you not realized that I commanded the people with a matter, yet they are hesitating?” Al-Hakam said: It is as though they were hesitating — I think so. “Had I known beforehand what I came to know later, I would not have brought the sacrificial animals with me until I bought them here, and then I would have come out of ihram as they did.”

وفي رواية عند مسلم (١٣٠)، عن عائشة، قالت: قَدِمَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ لِأَرْبَعٍ مَضَيْنَ مِنْ ذِي الْحِجَّةِ أَوْ خَمْسٍ، فَدَخَلَ عَلَيَّ وَهُوَ غَضْبَانُ، فَقُلْتُ: مَنْ أَغْضَبَكَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ؟ أَدْخَلَهُ اللَّهُ النَّارَ. قَالَ: (( أَوَمَا شَعَرْتِ أَنِّي أَمَرْتُ النَّاسَ بِأَمْرٍ، فَإِذَا هُمْ يَتَرَدَّدُونَ؟ )) قَالَ الْحَكَمُ: كَأَنَّهُمْ يَتَرَدَّدُونَ. أَحْسِبُ. (( وَلَوْ أَنِّي اسْتَقْبَلْتُ مِنْ أَمْرِي مَا اسْتَدْبَرْتُ، مَا سُقْتُ الْهَدْيَ مَعِي حَتَّى أَشْتَرِيَهُ، ثُمَّ أَحِلُّ كَمَا حَلُّوا )).

4913 — The Mother of the Believers, ‘A’ishah, said: We went out with the Prophet ﷺ not thinking it was anything but Hajj. Then when we arrived, we circled the House. The Prophet ﷺ ordered whoever had not brought sacrificial animals to come out of ihram, so those who had not brought sacrificial animals came out of ihram. And his wives had not brought sacrificial animals, so they too came out of ihram.

Agreed upon: narrated by al-Bukhari (1561) and Muslim (1211/128).

And in a narration in Muslim (130), from ‘A’ishah, she said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived on the fourth or fifth of Dhu al-Hijjah, and he entered upon me while angry. So I said: Who angered you, O Messenger of Allah ﷺ? May Allah enter him into the Fire. He said: “Have you not realized that I commanded the people with a matter, yet they are hesitating?” Al-Hakam said: It is as though they were hesitating — I think so. “Had I known beforehand what I came to know later, I would not have brought the sacrificial animals with me until I bought them here, and then I would have come out of ihram as they did.”

4914 — ‘A’ishah said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ thinking only of Hajj, until we came to Sarif and I menstruated. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon me while I was crying, and he said: “What makes you cry?” I said: By Allah, I wish I had not gone out this year. He said: “What is the matter? Perhaps you have begun menstruating?” I said: Yes. He said: “This is something Allah has decreed upon the daughters of Adam. 4916 — Abu Musa al-Ash‘ari said: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was camped at al-Batha’, and he said: “With what did you enter ihram?” I said: I entered ihram with the same ihram as the Prophet ﷺ. He said: “Did you bring any sacrificial animals?” I said: No. He said: “Then circumambulate the House and go between al-Safa and al-Marwah, then come out of ihram.” So I circumambulated the House and went between al-Safa and al-Marwah, then I went to a woman from my people and she combed my hair and washed my head. I used to give legal verdicts to the people with that during the caliphate of Abu Bakr and during the caliphate of ‘Umar. Then while I was in the pilgrimage season, a man came to me and said: You do not know what the Commander of the Believers has newly decided regarding the rites. So I said: O people, whoever we have given a ruling to about something, let him wait, for here is the Commander of the Believers coming to you, so follow him in this matter. Then when he came, I said: O Commander of the Believers, what is this that you have newly decided regarding the rites? He said: If we follow the Book of Allah, then Allah the Mighty and Majestic has said, “Complete the Hajj and Umrah for Allah.” And if we follow the Sunnah of our Prophet ﷺ, then the Prophet ﷺ did not come out of ihram until he slaughtered the sacrificial animals.

Agreed upon: narrated by al-Bukhari (1559) and Muslim (1221/155). The wording is that of Muslim.

And in another narration in Muslim (1222), from Abu Musa: that he used to give verdicts allowing tamattu‘, so a man said to him: “Slow down concerning some of your rulings, for you do not know what the Commander of the Believers has newly decided concerning the rites after that.” Then later he met him and asked him, and ‘Umar said: I knew that the Prophet ﷺ had done it, and his Companions as well, but I disliked that they should remain with their wives under the arak trees, then go out for Hajj while water still dripped from their heads.

وفي رواية لمسلم أيضاً (١٢٢٢) عن أبي موسى؛ أنه كان يفتي بالمتعة، فقال له رجل: (( رُوَيْدَكَ بَعْضَ فُتْيَاكَ، فَإِنَّكَ لا تَدْرِي مَا أَحْدَثَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ فِي النُّسُكِ بَعْدُ )). حَتَّى لَقِيَهُ بَعْدُ، فَسَأَلَهُ، فَقَالَ عُمَرُ: قَدْ عَلِمْتُ أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ قَدْ فَعَلَهُ وَأَصْحَابُهُ، وَلَكِنْ كَرِهْتُ أَنْ يَظَلُّوا مُعَرِّسِينَ بِهِنَّ فِي الْأَرَاكِ، ثُمَّ يَرُوحُونَ فِي الْحَجِّ تَقْطُرُ رُؤُوسُهُمْ.

4916 — Abu Musa al-Ash‘ari said: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was camped at al-Batha’, and he said: “With what did you enter ihram?” I said: I entered ihram with the same ihram as the Prophet ﷺ. He said: “Did you bring any sacrificial animals?” I said: No. He said: “Then circumambulate the House and go between al-Safa and al-Marwah, then come out of ihram.” So I circumambulated the House and went between al-Safa and al-Marwah, then I went to a woman from my people and she combed my hair and washed my head. I used to give legal verdicts to the people with that during the caliphate of Abu Bakr and during the caliphate of ‘Umar. Then while I was in the pilgrimage season, a man came to me and said: You do not know what the Commander of the Believers has newly decided regarding the rites. So I said: O people, whoever we have given a ruling to about something, let him wait, for here is the Commander of the Believers coming to you, so follow him in this matter. Then when he came, I said: O Commander of the Believers, what is this that you have newly decided regarding the rites? He said: If we follow the Book of Allah, then Allah the Mighty and Majestic has said, “Complete the Hajj and Umrah for Allah.” And if we follow the Sunnah of our Prophet ﷺ, then the Prophet ﷺ did not come out of ihram until he slaughtered the sacrificial animals.

Agreed upon: narrated by al-Bukhari (1559) and Muslim (1221/155). The wording is that of Muslim.

And in another narration in Muslim (1222), from Abu Musa: that he used to give verdicts allowing tamattu‘, so a man said to him: “Slow down concerning some of your rulings, for you do not know what the Commander of the Believers has newly decided concerning the rites after that.” Then later he met him and asked him, and ‘Umar said: I knew that the Prophet ﷺ had done it, and his Companions as well, but I disliked that they should remain with their wives under the arak trees, then go out for Hajj while water still dripped from their heads.

صحيح: رواه البخاري (٤٣٥٤، ٤٣٥٣).

٤٩١٨ — عن أسماء بنت أبي بكر، قالت: خَرَجْنَا مُحْرِمِينَ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: (( مَنْ كَانَ مَعَهُ هَدْيٌ فَلْيُقِمْ عَلَى إِحْرَامِهِ، وَمَنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ مَعَهُ هَدْيٌ فَلْيَحْلِلْ )). فَلَمْ يَكُنْ مَعِي هَدْيٌ فَحَلَلْتُ، وَكَانَ مَعَ الزُّبَيْرِ هَدْيٌ فَلَمْ يَحِلَّ. قَالَتْ: فَلَبِسْتُ ثِيَابِي، ثُمَّ خَرَجْتُ فَجَلَسْتُ إِلَى الزُّبَيْرِ، فَقَالَ: قُومِي عَنِّي.

صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٢٣٦).

وروى ابن أبي شيبة في مصنفه (١٠٣/٤) قال عبد الله بن الزبير: أفردوا الحجّ، ودعوا قول أعمىكم هذا! قال عبد الله بن عباس: إن الذي أعمى الله قلبه لأنت، ألا تسأل أمك عن هذا؟! فأرسل إليها، فقالت: صَدَقَ ابن عباس، خرجنا مع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ حجاجًا، فجعلناها عمرة، فحللنا الإحلال كلَّه حتى سطعت المجامر بين الرجال والنساء.

وقوله: (( سطعت )) أي ارتفعت، أي تداولوها بينهم للتبخّر بها.

4918 — Asma’ bint Abi Bakr said: We went out in ihram, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever has sacrificial animals with him should remain in his ihram, and whoever does not have sacrificial animals with him should come out of ihram.” I did not have sacrificial animals with me, so I came out of ihram, while al-Zubayr had sacrificial animals with him, so he did not come out of ihram. She said: So I put on my clothes, then I went out and sat beside al-Zubayr, and he said: Move away from me.

Authentic: narrated by Muslim (1236).

Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated in his Musannaf (4/103) that ‘Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr said: Make Hajj alone, and leave the statement of this blind man of yours. ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas said: Rather, you are the one whose heart Allah has blinded. Why do you not ask your mother about this? So he sent to her, and she said: Ibn ‘Abbas spoke the truth. We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as pilgrims, then we made it Umrah, and we came out of ihram completely, until incense burners were raised among the men and women.

His statement, “sat‘at,” means they were raised up, meaning the incense burners were passed around among them for perfuming themselves.

4918 — Asma’ bint Abi Bakr said: We went out in ihram, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever has sacrificial animals with him should remain in his ihram, and whoever does not have sacrificial animals with him should come out of ihram.” I did not have sacrificial animals with me, so I came out of ihram, while al-Zubayr had sacrificial animals with him, so he did not come out of ihram. She said: So I put on my clothes, then I went out and sat beside al-Zubayr, and he said: Move away from me.

Authentic: narrated by Muslim (1236).

Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated in his Musannaf (4/103) that ‘Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr said: Make Hajj alone, and leave the statement of this blind man of yours. ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas said: Rather, you are the one whose heart Allah has blinded. Why do you not ask your mother about this? So he sent to her, and she said: Ibn ‘Abbas spoke the truth. We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as pilgrims, then we made it Umrah, and we came out of ihram completely, until incense burners were raised among the men and women.

His statement, “sat‘at,” means they were raised up, meaning the incense burners were passed around among them for perfuming themselves.

٤٩١٩ — عن ابن عباس، قال: كَانُوا يَرَوْنَ أَنَّ الْعُمْرَةَ فِي أَشْهُرِ الْحَجِّ مِنْ أَفْجَرِ الْفُجُورِ فِي الأَرْضِ، وَيَجْعَلُونَ الْمُحَرَّمَ صَفَرًا، وَيَقُولُونَ: إِذَا بَرَأَ الدَّبَرُ، وَعَفَا الأَثَرُ، وَانْسَلَخَ صَفَرُ، حَلَّتِ الْعُمْرَةُ لِمَنِ اعْتَمَرَ. فَقَدِمَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ وَأَصْحَابُهُ صَبِيحَةَ رَابِعَةٍ مُهِلِّينَ بِالْحَجِّ، فَأَمَرَهُمْ أَنْ يَجْعَلُوهَا عُمْرَةً، فَتَعَاظَمَ ذَلِكَ عِنْدَهُمْ، فَقَالُوا: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، أَيُّ الْحِلِّ؟ قَالَ: (( حِلٌّ كُلُّهُ )).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاريّ (١٥٦٤)، ومسلم (١٢٤٠).

Agreed upon: narrated by al-Bukhari (1564) and Muslim (1240).

٤٩٢٠ — عن عبد الله بن عباس، قال: قَدِمَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ وَأَصْحَابُهُ لِصُبْحِ رَابِعَةٍ يُلَبُّونَ بِالْحَجِّ، فَأَمَرَهُمْ أَنْ يَجْعَلُوهَا عُمْرَةً إِلَّا مَنْ مَعَهُ الْهَدْيُ.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٠٨٥)، ومسلم (٢٠٢ :١٢٤٠). واللفظ للبخاري، ولفظ مسلم: (( أن يحوّلوا إحرامهم بعمرة إلا من كان معه الهدي )).

4920 — ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas said: The Prophet ﷺ and his Companions arrived on the morning of the fourth while reciting the talbiyah for Hajj, and he ordered them to make it Umrah, except for those who had sacrificial animals with them.

٤٩٢١ — عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما، أنه سُئِلَ عن متعة الحج، فقال: أَهَلَّ الْمُهَاجِرُونَ وَالأَنْصَارُ وَأَزْوَاجُ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ فِي حَجَّةِ الْوَدَاعِ، وَأَهْلَلْنَا، فَلَمَّا قَدِمْنَا مَكَّةَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: (( اجْعَلُوا إِهْلالَكُمْ بِالْحَجِّ عُمْرَةً إِلَّا مَنْ قَلَّدَ الْهَدْيَ )). فَطُفْنَا بِالْبَيْتِ وَبِالصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ، وَأَتَيْنَا النِّسَاءَ، وَلَبِسْنَا الثِّيَابَ، وَقَالَ: (( مَنْ قَلَّدَ الْهَدْيَ، فَإِنَّهُ لا يَحِلُّ لَهُ حَتَّى يَبْلُغَ الْهَدْيُ مَحِلَّهُ )). ثُمَّ أَمَرَنَا عَشِيَّةَ التَّرْوِيَةِ أَنْ نُهِلَّ بِالْحَجِّ، فَإِذَا فَرَغْنَا مِنَ الْمَنَاسِكِ جِئْنَا فَطُفْنَا بِالْبَيْتِ وَبِالصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ، فَقَدْ تَمَّ حَجُّنَا وَعَلَيْنَا الْهَدْيُ، كَمَا قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: (فَمَا اسْتَيْسَرَ مِنَ الْهَدْيِ فَمَنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيَامُ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ فِي الْحَجِّ وَسَبْعَةٍ إِذَا رَجَعْتُمْ) إِلَى أَمْصَارِكُمْ. الشَّاةُ تُجْزِئُ، فَجَمَعُوا نُسُكَيْنِ فِي عَامٍ بَيْنَ الْحَجِّ وَالْعُمْرَةِ، فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى أَنْزَلَهُ فِي كِتَابِهِ، وَسَنَّهُ نَبِيُّهُ ﷺ، وَأَبَاحَهُ لِلنَّاسِ غَيْرَ أَهْلِ مَكَّةَ. قَالَ اللَّهُ: (ذَٰلِكَ لِمَنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ أَهْلُهُ حَاضِرِي الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ). وَأَشْهُرُ الْحَجِّ الَّتِي ذَكَرَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى فِي كِتَابِهِ: شَوَّالٌ، وَذُو الْقَعْدَةِ، وَذُو الْحِجَّةِ، فَمَنْ تَمَتَّعَ فِي هَذِهِ الأَشْهُرِ فَعَلَيْهِ دَمٌ أَوْ صَوْمٌ، وَالرَّفَثُ: الْجِمَاعُ، وَالْفُسُوقُ: الْمَعَاصِي، وَالْجِدَالُ: الْمِرَاءُ.

4921 — ‘Ikrimah narrated from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he was asked about tamattu‘ in Hajj, so he said: The Emigrants, the Helpers, and the wives of the Prophet ﷺ entered ihram in the Farewell Pilgrimage, and we entered ihram as well. Then when we came to Makkah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Make your ihram for Hajj into an Umrah, except for the one who has garlanded the sacrificial animal.” So we circumambulated the House and went between al-Safa and al-Marwah, we went to our women, and we wore regular clothes. And he said: “Whoever has garlanded the sacrificial animal, it is not lawful for him to come out of ihram until the sacrificial animal reaches its place of slaughter.” Then on the evening before the Day of Tarwiyah he ordered us to enter ihram for Hajj. Then when we finished the rites, we came and circumambulated the House and went between al-Safa and al-Marwah, and our Hajj was complete, and the sacrificial offering was due from us, just as Allah Most High said: “Then whatever can be obtained with ease of sacrificial animals; and whoever cannot find one, then fasting three days during Hajj and seven when you return” to your homelands. One sheep suffices. Thus they combined two rites in one year: Hajj and Umrah. Allah Most High revealed it in His Book, His Prophet ﷺ established it as Sunnah, and He permitted it for the people other than the people of Makkah. Allah said: “That is for the one whose family are not residents near the Sacred Mosque.” And the months of Hajj that Allah mentioned in His Book are Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa‘dah, and Dhu al-Hijjah. So whoever performs tamattu‘ in these months must offer a sacrifice or fast. And “obscene speech” means sexual intercourse, “sinfulness” means acts of disobedience, and “argumentation” means disputation.

صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٢٣٩).

٤٩٢٤ — عن ابن عباس، أنه كان يقول: لا يطوفُ بالبيت حاجٌّ ولا غيرُ حاجٍّ إلا حلَّ. قلتُ (أي ابن جريج) لعطاء: مِن أين يقول ذلك؟ قال: مِن قولِ الله تعالى: { ثُمَّ مَحِلُّهَا إِلَى الْبَيْتِ الْعَتِيقِ }. قال: قلتُ: فإنَّ ذلك بعدَ المُعَرَّفِ؟ فقال: كان ابن عباس يقول: هو بعد المُعَرَّفِ وقبلَهُ. وكان يأخذ ذلك من أمرِ النبيِّ ﷺ حين أمرهم أن يحلُّوا في حجَّة الوداع.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاريّ (٤٣٩٦)، ومسلم (١٢٤٥). واللفظ لمسلم.

english_source:
4924 — Ibn ‘Abbas used to say: No one, whether a pilgrim or otherwise, circles the House except that he comes out of ihram. Ibn Jurayj said: I asked ‘Ata’: From where did he say that? He said: From the saying of Allah Most High: “Then their place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House.” I said: But is that not after standing at ‘Arafah? He said: Ibn ‘Abbas used to say: It is after standing at ‘Arafah and before it. And he took that from the command of the Prophet ﷺ when he ordered them to come out of ihram during the Farewell Pilgrimage.

Agreed upon: narrated by al-Bukhari (4396) and Muslim (1245). The wording is that of Muslim.

٤٩٢٥ — عن كريب مولى عبد الله بن عباس، عن عبد الله بن عباس، قال: قلت له: يا أبا العباس، أرأيتَ قولَك: ما حجَّ رجلٌ لم يسقِ الهديَ معه ثم طاف بالبيت إلا حلَّ بعمرة، وما طاف بها حاجٌّ قد ساق معه الهدي إلا اجتمعت له عمرةٌ وحجَّةٌ، والناس لا يقولون هذا؟ فقال: ويحك، إنَّ رسول اللّٰه ﷺ خرج ومَن معه من أصحابه لا يذكرون إلا الحج، فأمر رسول اللّٰه ﷺ من لم يكن معه الهدي أن يطوف بالبيت ويحلَّ بعمرة، فجعل الرجل منهم يقول: يا رسول الله، إنما هو الحج؟ فيقول رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( إنَّه ليس بالحج، ولكنها عمرة )).

حسن: رواه أحمد (٢٣٦٠).

4925 — Kurayb, the freedman of ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas, narrated from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas that he said: I said to him: O Abu al-‘Abbas, what about your statement that no man who performs Hajj without bringing a sacrificial animal and then circumambulates the House except that he comes out of ihram as an Umrah pilgrim, and that no pilgrim who has brought a sacrificial animal circumambulates it except that Umrah and Hajj are joined together for him, while the people do not say this? He said: Woe to you. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out, and those with him among his Companions mentioned only Hajj. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded whoever did not have a sacrificial animal with him to circumambulate the House and come out of ihram as an Umrah pilgrim. Then one of them would say: O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, it is only Hajj. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would say: “It is not Hajj only; rather, it is an Umrah.”

Hasan: narrated by Ahmad (2360).

٤٩٢٦ — عن جابر بن عبد الله، قال: قدمنا مع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ ونحن نقول: لبيك اللهم لبيك بالحج، فأمرنا رسولُ اللّٰه ﷺ فجعلناها عمرةً.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٥٧٠)، ومسلم (١٢١٦)، واللفظ للبخاريّ.

٤٩٢٧ — عن جابر، قال: قدم النبيُّ ﷺ وأصحابُه صبحَ رابعةٍ من ذي الحجة مُهِلِّين بالحج لا يخلطهم شيء، فلما قدمنا أمرنا فجعلناها عمرةً، وأن نحلَّ إلى نسائنا، ففشت في ذلك القالة. قال عطاء: فقال جابر: فيروح أحدنا إلى منى وذكرُه يقطر منيًّا. فقال جابر بكفِّه. فبلغ ذلك النبيَّ ﷺ، فقام خطيبًا فقال: (( بلغني أنَّ أقوامًا يقولون كذا وكذا، واللهِ لأنا أبرُّ وأتقى لله منهم، ولو أني استقبلتُ من أمري ما استدبرتُ ما أهديتُ، ولولا أن معي الهدي لأحللتُ )). فقام سراقة بن مالك بن جعشم، فقال: يا رسول الله، هي لنا أو للأبد؟ فقال: (( لا، بل للأبد )).

٤٩٢٩ — عن ابن عمر، أنّ حفصة زوج النبيِّ ﷺ قالت: يا رسول الله، ما شأنُ الناس حلُّوا ولم تحللْ أنتَ من عمرتك؟ قال: (( إنّي لبَّدتُ رأسي، وقلَّدتُ هديي، فلا أحلُّ حتى أنحر )).

٤٩٣٠ — عن أبي سعيد، قال: خرجنا مع رسولِ اللّٰه ﷺ نصرخ بالحجِّ صراخًا، فلما قدمنا مكة أمرنا أن نجعلها عمرةً إلا من ساق الهدي، فلما كان يوم التروية ورحنا إلى منى أهللنا بالحجِّ.

صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٢٤٧).

٤٩٣١ — عن سراقة بن جُعشم، قال: قام رسولُ اللّٰه ﷺ خطيبًا في هذا الوادي فقال: (( ألا إنَّ العمرة قد دخلتْ في الحجِّ إلى يوم القيامة )).

صحيح: رواه ابن ماجه (٢٩٧٧)، والنسائي (٢٨٠٦)، واللفظ لابن ماجه.

Authentic: narrated by Ibn Majah (2977) and al-Nasa’i (2806). The wording is that of Ibn Majah.

٤٩٣٢ — عن الرَّبيع بن سبرة، عن أبيه، قال: خرجنا مع رسولِ اللّٰه ﷺ حتى إذا كان بعُسفان قال له سراقة بن مالك المُدلجي: يا رسول الله، اقضِ لنا قضاءَ قومٍ كأنما وُلِدوا اليوم. فقال: (( إنَّ الله تعالى قد أدخل عليكم في حجِّكم هذا عمرةً، فإذا قدمتم فمَن تطوَّف بالبيت وبين الصفا والمروة فقد حلَّ، إلا مَن كان معه هديٌ )).

صحيح: رواه أبو داود (١٨٠١)، وعبد الرزاق (١٤٠٤١)، والإمام أحمد (١٥٣٤٥).

4932 — Al-Rabi‘ ibn Sabrah narrated from his father, who said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until, when we were at ‘Usfan, Suraqah ibn Malik al-Mudliji said to him: O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, give us a ruling like the ruling for a people as though they were born today. So he said: “Allah the Exalted has entered an Umrah into this Hajj of yours. So when you arrive, whoever circumambulates the House and goes between al-Safa and al-Marwah has come out of ihram, except for the one who has a sacrificial animal with him.”

Authentic: narrated by Abu Dawud (1801), ‘Abd al-Razzaq (14041), and Ahmad (15345).

٤٩٣٣ — عن البراء بن عازب قال: كُنْتُ مَعَ عَلِيٍّ حِينَ أَمَّرَهُ رَسُولُ اللّٰهِ ﷺ عَلَى الْيَمَنِ، قَالَ: فَأَصَبْتُ مَعَهُ أَوَاقِيَ، فَلَمَّا قَدِمَ عَلِيٌّ مِنَ الْيَمَنِ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللّٰهِ ﷺ قَالَ: وَجَدْتُ فَاطِمَةَ رَضِيَ اللّٰهُ عَنْهَا قَدْ لَبِسَتْ ثِيَابًا صَبِيغًا، وَقَدْ نَضَحَتِ الْبَيْتَ بِنَضُوحٍ، فَقَالَتْ: مَا لَكَ؟ فَإِنَّ رَسُولَ اللّٰهِ ﷺ قَدْ أَمَرَ أَصْحَابَهُ فَأَحَلُّوا.

قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهَا: إِنِّي أَهْلَلْتُ بِإِهْلَالِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ.

قَالَ: فَأَتَيْتُ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ فَقَالَ لِي: (( كَيْفَ صَنَعْتَ؟ )).

فَقَالَ: قُلْتُ: أَهْلَلْتُ بِإِهْلَالِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ.

قَالَ: (( فَإِنِّي قَدْ سُقْتُ الْهَدْيَ وَقَرَنْتُ )).

قَالَ: فَقَالَ لِي: (( انْحَرْ مِنَ الْبُدْنِ سَبْعًا وَسِتِّينَ أَوْ سِتًّا وَسِتِّينَ، وَأَمْسِكْ لِنَفْسِكَ ثَلَاثًا وَثَلَاثِينَ أَوْ أَرْبَعًا وَثَلَاثِينَ، وَأَمْسِكْ لِي مِنْ كُلِّ بَدَنَةٍ مِنْهَا بَضْعَةً )).

حسن: رواه أبو داود (١٧٩٧)، والنسائيّ (٢٧٤٥).

4933 — Al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib said: I was with ‘Ali when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed him over Yemen. He said: I acquired some awqiyah with him. When ‘Ali came from Yemen to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said: I found Fatimah, may Allah be pleased with her, wearing dyed clothes and having perfumed the house. She said: What is the matter with you? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had commanded his companions to exit ihram, and they did so.

He said: I told her, “I entered ihram with the same intention as the Prophet ﷺ.”

He said: So I came to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said to me, “What did you do?”

He said: I replied, “I entered ihram with the same intention as the Prophet ﷺ.”

He said: “I have brought the sacrificial animals and have combined Hajj and Umrah.”

He said: Then he said to me: “Slaughter sixty-seven or sixty-six of the camels, keep thirty-three or thirty-four for yourself, and keep for me a piece from each camel.”

Hasan: Narrated by Abu Dawud (1797) and al-Nasa’i (2745).

٤٩٣٣ — عن البراء بن عازب قال: كُنْتُ مَعَ عَلِيٍّ حِينَ أَمَّرَهُ رَسُولُ اللّٰهِ ﷺ عَلَى الْيَمَنِ، قَالَ: فَأَصَبْتُ مَعَهُ أَوَاقِيَ، فَلَمَّا قَدِمَ عَلِيٌّ مِنَ الْيَمَنِ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللّٰهِ ﷺ قَالَ: وَجَدْتُ فَاطِمَةَ رَضِيَ اللّٰهُ عَنْهَا قَدْ لَبِسَتْ ثِيَابًا صَبِيغًا، وَقَدْ نَضَحَتِ الْبَيْتَ بِنَضُوحٍ، فَقَالَتْ: مَا لَكَ؟ فَإِنَّ رَسُولَ اللّٰهِ ﷺ قَدْ أَمَرَ أَصْحَابَهُ فَأَحَلُّوا.

قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهَا: إِنِّي أَهْلَلْتُ بِإِهْلَالِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ.

قَالَ: فَأَتَيْتُ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ فَقَالَ لِي: (( كَيْفَ صَنَعْتَ؟ )).

فَقَالَ: قُلْتُ: أَهْلَلْتُ بِإِهْلَالِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ.

قَالَ: (( فَإِنِّي قَدْ سُقْتُ الْهَدْيَ وَقَرَنْتُ )).

قَالَ: فَقَالَ لِي: (( انْحَرْ مِنَ الْبُدْنِ سَبْعًا وَسِتِّينَ أَوْ سِتًّا وَسِتِّينَ، وَأَمْسِكْ لِنَفْسِكَ ثَلَاثًا وَثَلَاثِينَ أَوْ أَرْبَعًا وَثَلَاثِينَ، وَأَمْسِكْ لِي مِنْ كُلِّ بَدَنَةٍ مِنْهَا بَضْعَةً )).

حسن: رواه أبو داود (١٧٩٧)، والنسائيّ (٢٧٤٥).

4933 — Al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib said: I was with ‘Ali when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed him over Yemen. He said: I acquired some awqiyah with him. When ‘Ali came from Yemen to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said: I found Fatimah, may Allah be pleased with her, wearing dyed clothes and having perfumed the house. She said: What is the matter with you? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had commanded his companions to exit ihram, and they did so.

He said: I told her, “I entered ihram with the same intention as the Prophet ﷺ.”

He said: So I came to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said to me, “What did you do?”

He said: I replied, “I entered ihram with the same intention as the Prophet ﷺ.”

He said: “I have brought the sacrificial animals and have combined Hajj and Umrah.”

He said: Then he said to me: “Slaughter sixty-seven or sixty-six of the camels, keep thirty-three or thirty-four for yourself, and keep for me a piece from each camel.”

Hasan: Narrated by Abu Dawud (1797) and al-Nasa’i (2745).

٤٩٣٤ — عن عمران بن حصين، قال: أُنزِلَتْ آيَةُ الْمُتْعَةِ فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ فَفَعَلْنَاهَا مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ، وَلَمْ يُنْزَلْ قُرْآنٌ يُحَرِّمُهُ، وَلَمْ يَنْهَ عَنْهَا حَتَّى مَاتَ، قَالَ رَجُلٌ بِرَأْيِهِ مَا شَاءَ.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاريّ (٤٥١٨)، ومسلم (١٧٢:١٢٢٦)، واللفظ للبخاريّ. وفي لفظ مسلم: (( ثُمَّ لَمْ تَنْزِلْ آيَةٌ تَنْسَخُ آيَةَ مُتْعَةِ الْحَجِّ )). وفي الصحيحين أيضًا: البخاري (١٥٧١)، ومسلم (١٧:١٢٢٦)، عن عمران بن حصين، قال: (( تَمَتَّعْنَا عَلَى عَهْدِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ، فَنَزَلَ الْقُرْآنُ، قَالَ رَجُلٌ بِرَأْيِهِ مَا شَاءَ )).

وقوله: (( قال رجل برأيه ما شاء )) يقصد به عمر بن الخطاب، فإنه كان ينهى عن المتعة اجتهادًا.

english_source:
4934 — ‘Imran ibn Husayn said: The verse of tamattu‘ was revealed in the Book of Allah, and we practiced it with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. No Qur’an was revealed to forbid it, and he did not forbid it until he died. Then a man said whatever he wished based on his own opinion.

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (4518) and Muslim (1226:172), and this wording is that of al-Bukhari. In the wording of Muslim: “Then no verse was revealed abrogating the verse of tamattu‘ in Hajj.” In the two Sahihs as well: al-Bukhari (1571) and Muslim (1226:17), from ‘Imran ibn Husayn, who said: “We performed tamattu‘ during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Qur’an was revealed; then a man said whatever he wished based on his own opinion.”

His statement, “Then a man said whatever he wished based on his own opinion,” refers to ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, for he used to discourage tamattu‘ as a matter of juristic judgment.

٤٩٣٥ — عن مروان بن الحكم، قال: شَهِدْتُ عُثْمَانَ وَعَلِيًّا رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا، وَعُثْمَانُ يَنْهَى عَنِ الْمُتْعَةِ وَأَنْ يُجْمَعَ بَيْنَهُمَا، فَلَمَّا رَأَى عَلِيٌّ أَهَلَّ بِهِمَا: لَبَّيْكَ بِعُمْرَةٍ وَحَجَّةٍ، قَالَ: مَا كُنْتُ لِأَدَعَ سُنَّةَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ لِقَوْلِ أَحَدٍ.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٥٦٣) والبخاري أيضًا (١٥٦٩)، ومسلم (١٢٢٣). وفيه: اجتمع عليٌّ وعثمان رضي اللّٰه عنهما بعسفان، فكان عثمان ينهى عن المتعة أو العمرة. فقال عليٌّ: ما تريد إلى أمر فعله رسول الله ﷺ تنهى عنه؟! فقال عثمان: دعنا منك. فقال: إني لا أستطيع أن أدعك. فلما أن رأى عليٌّ ذلك أهلَّ بهما جميعًا. واللفظ لمسلم.

ورواه مسلم أيضًا وفيه: كان عثمان ينهى عن المتعة، وكان عليٌّ يأمر بها، فقال عثمان لعليّ كلمة، ثم قال عليٌّ: لقد علمتَ أنّا قد تمتعنا مع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ؟ فقال: أجل، ولكنّا كنّا خائفين.

4935 — Marwan ibn al-Hakam said: I witnessed ‘Uthman and ‘Ali, may Allah be pleased with them both, while ‘Uthman was discouraging tamattu‘ and combining the two rites. When ‘Ali saw that, he entered ihram for both, saying: “Here I am for Umrah and Hajj.” He said: “I would never abandon the Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ for the statement of anyone.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (1563), also by al-Bukhari (1569), and Muslim (1223). In it: ‘Ali and ‘Uthman, may Allah be pleased with them, met at ‘Usfan, and ‘Uthman was discouraging tamattu‘ or Umrah. ‘Ali said: “Why do you oppose something the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did?” ‘Uthman said: “Leave us alone.” ‘Ali said: “I cannot leave you alone.” When ‘Ali saw that, he entered ihram for both together. This is the wording of Muslim.

Muslim also narrated that ‘Uthman was discouraging tamattu‘ while ‘Ali used to command it. Then ‘Uthman said something to ‘Ali, and ‘Ali replied: “You certainly know that we performed tamattu‘ with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.” He said: “Yes, but at that time we were afraid.”

٤٩٣٦ — عن نصر بن عمران أبي جمرة الضُّبَعي، قال: تَمَتَّعْتُ فَنَهَانِي نَاسٌ عَنْ ذَلِكَ، فَأَتَيْتُ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ فَسَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ ذَلِكَ فَأَمَرَنِي بِهَا.

قَالَ: ثُمَّ انْطَلَقْتُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ فَنِمْتُ، فَأَتَانِي آتٍ فِي مَنَامِي، فَقَالَ: عُمْرَةٌ مُتَقَبَّلَةٌ وَحَجٌّ مَبْرُورٌ.

قَالَ: فَأَتَيْتُ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ فَأَخْبَرْتُهُ بِالَّذِي رَأَيْتُ، فَقَالَ: اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ! اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ! سُنَّةُ أَبِي الْقَاسِمِ ﷺ.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاريّ (١٥٦٧)، ومسلم (١٢٤٢). واللفظ لمسلم، ولفظ البخاري نحوه، وزاد: (( فقال لي: أَقِمْ عندي فأجعل لك سهمًا من مالي )). قال شعبة: فقلتُ: لِمَ؟ فقال: للرؤيا التي رأيتُ.

4936 — Nasr ibn ‘Imran Abu Jamrah al-Duba‘i said: I performed tamattu‘, and some people forbade me from doing that. So I went to Ibn ‘Abbas and asked him about it, and he instructed me to do it.

He said: Then I went to the House and slept, and someone came to me in my dream and said: “An accepted Umrah and a blessed Hajj.”

He said: So I went to Ibn ‘Abbas and informed him of what I had seen, and he said: “Allah is the Greatest! Allah is the Greatest! This is the Sunnah of Abu al-Qasim ﷺ.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (1567) and Muslim (1242). This wording is that of Muslim. The wording of al-Bukhari is similar, with the addition: “He said to me: Stay with me and I will assign you a share from my wealth.” Shu‘bah said: I asked, “Why?” He replied: “Because of the dream that you saw.”

٤٩٣٧ — عن مسلم القُرِّيِّ، قال: سَأَلْتُ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا عَنْ مُتْعَةِ الْحَجِّ، فَرَخَّصَ فِيهَا، وَكَانَ ابْنُ الزُّبَيْرِ يَنْهَى عَنْهَا، فَقَالَ: هَذِهِ أُمُّ ابْنِ الزُّبَيْرِ تُحَدِّثُ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ رَخَّصَ فِيهَا، فَادْخُلُوا عَلَيْهَا فَاسْأَلُوهَا.

قَالَ: فَدَخَلْنَا عَلَيْهَا، فَإِذَا امْرَأَةٌ ضَخْمَةٌ عَمْيَاءُ، فَقَالَتْ: قَدْ رَخَّصَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ فِيهَا.

4937 — Muslim al-Qurri said: I asked Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, about tamattu‘ in Hajj, and he allowed it, while Ibn al-Zubayr used to forbid it. So he said: “This is the mother of Ibn al-Zubayr narrating that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ permitted it. Go in to her and ask her.”

He said: So we went in to her, and there she was, a large blind woman, and she said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did indeed permit it.”

Sahih: Narrated by Muslim (1238).

٤٩٣٨ — عن غُنَيْمِ بْنِ قَيْسٍ، قال: سَأَلْتُ سَعْدَ بْنَ أَبِي وَقَّاصٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ عَنِ الْمُتْعَةِ؟ فَقَالَ: فَعَلْنَاهَا وَهَذَا يَوْمَئِذٍ كَافِرٌ بِالْعُرُشِ - يَعْنِي بُيُوتَ مَكَّةَ -.

صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٢٢٥).

قوله: (( عن المتعة )) يعني المتعة في الحج - كما في رواية -، والمراد بالحج هنا: العمرة؛ لأنهم كانوا يطلقون الحج على العمرة.

وقوله: (( وهذا يومئذ كافر بالعُرُش )) العُرُش - بضم العين والراء -: وهي بيوت مكة كما فُسِّر في الرواية.

قال أبو عبيد: (( سُمِّيَتْ بُيُوتُ مَكَّةَ عُرُوشًا؛ لِأَنَّهَا عِيدَانٌ تُنْصَبُ وَتُظَلَّلُ )).

قال النووي: (( والإشارة بهذا إلى معاوية بن أبي سفيان، والمراد: أنّا تمتعنا ومعاوية يومئذ كافر على دين الجاهلية مقيم بمكة. والمراد بالمتعة العمرة التي كانت سنة سبع من الهجرة، وهي عمرة القضاء، وكان معاوية يومئذ كافرًا، وإنما أسلم بعد ذلك عام الفتح سنة ثمان، وقيل: إنه أسلم بعد عمرة القضاء سنة سبع، والصحيح الأول. وأما غير هذه العمرة من عمر النبي ﷺ فلم يكن معاوية فيها كافرًا ولا مقيمًا بمكة، بل كان معه ﷺ )). قال: (( وفي هذا الحديث جواز المتعة في الحج )). انظر شرح مسلم (٨/٢٠٣-٢٠٤).

4938 — Ghunaym ibn Qays said: I asked Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas, may Allah be pleased with him, about tamattu‘. He said: “We did it while this man at that time was still a disbeliever among the shelters,” meaning the houses of Makkah.

Sahih: Narrated by Muslim (1225).

His statement, “about tamattu‘,” means tamattu‘ in Hajj, as mentioned in another narration; here, however, Hajj refers to Umrah, because they would sometimes use the word Hajj to refer to Umrah.

His statement, “while this man at that time was still a disbeliever among the shelters,” means the houses of Makkah, as explained in the narration.

Abu ‘Ubayd said: “The houses of Makkah were called ‘urush because they were made of poles that were erected and shaded over.”

Al-Nawawi said: “The reference here is to Mu‘awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan. The meaning is: we performed tamattu‘ while Mu‘awiyah at that time was still a disbeliever upon the religion of the pre-Islamic period and residing in Makkah. What is meant by tamattu‘ here is the Umrah that occurred in the seventh year after migration, namely the make-up Umrah. Mu‘awiyah was a disbeliever at that time, and he only accepted Islam later in the year of the Conquest, year eight. It was also said that he accepted Islam after the make-up Umrah in year seven, but the first view is the correct one. As for the other ‘umrahs of the Prophet ﷺ, Mu‘awiyah was neither a disbeliever nor residing in Makkah during them; rather, he was with the Prophet ﷺ.” He also said: “This hadith proves the permissibility of tamattu‘ in Hajj.” See Sharh Muslim (8/203–204).

٤٩٣٩ — عن أبي هريرة، عن النبيِّ ﷺ قال: (( وَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ! لَيُهِلَّنَّ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ بِفَجِّ الرَّوْحَاءِ حَاجًّا أَوْ مُعْتَمِرًا أَوْ لَيَثْنِيَنَّهُمَا )).

صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٢٥٢).

قوله: (( لَيَثْنِيَنَّهُمَا )) هو بفتح الياء في أوله، معناه: يقرن بينهما، وهذا يكون بعد نزول عيسى عليه السلام من السماء في آخر الزمان. وأما فَجُّ الرَّوحاء فبفتح الفاء وتشديد الجيم، قال الحافظ أبو بكر الحازمي: موضع بين مكة والمدينة، قال: وكان طريق رسول الله ﷺ إلى بدر وإلى مكة عام الفتح، وعام حجة الوداع. انظر: شرح النووي على مسلم (٨/٢٣٣).

4939 — Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: “By the One in whose Hand is my soul, the son of Mary will certainly enter the mountain pass of al-Rawha’ proclaiming the pilgrimage, or the lesser pilgrimage, or he will combine the two.”

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1252).

His statement, “or he will combine the two,” means that he will combine the pilgrimage and the lesser pilgrimage together. This will happen after Jesus, peace be upon him, descends from heaven near the end of time. As for the pass of al-Rawha’, it is a place between Mecca and Medina. Abu Bakr al-Hazimi said it was on the route of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to Badr, to Mecca in the year of the Conquest, and in the Farewell Pilgrimage. See al-Nawawi’s commentary on Muslim (8/233).

قوله: (( لَيَثْنِيَنَّهُمَا )) هو بفتح الياء في أوله، معناه: يقرن بينهما، وهذا يكون بعد نزول عيسى عليه السلام من السماء في آخر الزمان. وأما فَجُّ الرَّوحاء فبفتح الفاء وتشديد الجيم، قال الحافظ أبو بكر الحازمي: موضع بين مكة والمدينة، قال: وكان طريق رسول الله ﷺ إلى بدر وإلى مكة عام الفتح، وعام حجة الوداع. انظر: شرح النووي على مسلم (٨/٢٣٣).

4939 — Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: “By the One in whose Hand is my soul, the son of Mary will certainly enter the mountain pass of al-Rawha’ proclaiming the pilgrimage, or the lesser pilgrimage, or he will combine the two.”

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1252).

His statement, “or he will combine the two,” means that he will combine the pilgrimage and the lesser pilgrimage together. This will happen after Jesus, peace be upon him, descends from heaven near the end of time. As for the pass of al-Rawha’, it is a place between Mecca and Medina. Abu Bakr al-Hazimi said it was on the route of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to Badr, to Mecca in the year of the Conquest, and in the Farewell Pilgrimage. See al-Nawawi’s commentary on Muslim (8/233).

٤٩٤٠ — عن محمد بن عبد الرحمن بن نوفل القرشي، أنه سأل عروة بن الزبير، فقال: قَدْ حَجَّ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ فَأَخْبَرَتْنِي عَائِشَةُ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا أَنَّهُ أَوَّلُ شَيْءٍ بَدَأَ بِهِ حِينَ قَدِمَ أَنَّهُ تَوَضَّأَ ثُمَّ طَافَ بِالْبَيْتِ، ثُمَّ لَمْ تَكُنْ عُمْرَةً، ثُمَّ حَجَّ أَبُو بَكْرٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ فَكَانَ أَوَّلَ شَيْءٍ بَدَأَ بِهِ الطَّوَافُ بِالْبَيْتِ، ثُمَّ لَمْ تَكُنْ عُمْرَةً، ثُمَّ عُمَرُ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ مِثْلُ ذَلِكَ، ثُمَّ حَجَّ عُثْمَانُ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ فَرَأَيْتُهُ أَوَّلَ شَيْءٍ بَدَأَ بِهِ الطَّوَافُ بِالْبَيْتِ، ثُمَّ لَمْ تَكُنْ عُمْرَةً، ثُمَّ مُعَاوِيَةُ وَعَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عُمَرَ، ثُمَّ حَجَجْتُ مَعَ أَبِي الزُّبَيْرِ بْنِ الْعَوَّامِ فَكَانَ أَوَّلَ شَيْءٍ بَدَأَ بِهِ الطَّوَافُ بِالْبَيْتِ، ثُمَّ لَمْ تَكُنْ عُمْرَةً، ثُمَّ رَأَيْتُ الْمُهَاجِرِينَ وَالْأَنْصَارَ يَفْعَلُونَ ذَلِكَ، ثُمَّ لَمْ تَكُنْ عُمْرَةً، ثُمَّ آخِرُ مَنْ رَأَيْتُ فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ ابْنُ عُمَرَ، ثُمَّ لَمْ يَنْقُضْهَا عُمْرَةً، وَهَذَا ابْنُ عُمَرَ عِنْدَهُمْ فَلَا يَسْأَلُونَهُ، وَلَا أَحَدٌ مِمَّنْ مَضَى مَا كَانُوا يَبْدَؤُونَ بِشَيْءٍ حَتَّى يَضَعُوا أَقْدَامَهُمْ مِنَ الطَّوَافِ بِالْبَيْتِ، ثُمَّ لَا يَحِلُّونَ، وَقَدْ رَأَيْتُ أُمِّي وَخَالَتِي حِينَ تَقْدَمَانِ لَا تَبْتَدِئَانِ بِشَيْءٍ أَوَّلَ مِنَ الْبَيْتِ تَطُوفَانِ بِهِ، ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمَا لَا تَحِلَّانِ، وَقَدْ أَخْبَرَتْنِي أُمِّي أَنَّهَا أَهَلَّتْ هِيَ وَأُخْتُهَا وَالزُّبَيْرُ وَفُلَانٌ وَفُلَانٌ بِعُمْرَةٍ، فَلَمَّا مَسَحُوا الرُّكْنَ حَلُّوا.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاريّ (١٦٤١)، ومسلم (١٢٣٥). وهذا لفظ البخاريّ.

4940 — Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Nawfal al-Qurashi reported that he asked ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, and he said: The Prophet ﷺ performed the pilgrimage, and ‘A’ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, informed me that the first thing he began with when he arrived was that he performed ablution, then circled the House, and that was not a lesser pilgrimage. Then Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, performed the pilgrimage, and the first thing he began with was circling the House, and that was not a lesser pilgrimage. Then ‘Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, did the same. Then ‘Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, performed the pilgrimage, and I saw that the first thing he began with was circling the House, and that was not a lesser pilgrimage. Then Mu‘awiyah and ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar did the same. Then I performed the pilgrimage with my father al-Zubayr ibn al-‘Awwam, and the first thing he began with was circling the House, and that was not a lesser pilgrimage. Then I saw the Emigrants and the Helpers doing that, and that was not a lesser pilgrimage. Then the last person I saw doing that was Ibn ‘Umar, and he did not turn it into a lesser pilgrimage. And here is Ibn ‘Umar among them, yet they do not ask him. No one from those who passed before would begin with anything before placing their feet in the circling of the House, then they would not exit the state of consecration. I also saw my mother and my aunt, when they arrived, not begin with anything before the House, circling it, and then they did not exit the state of consecration. My mother informed me that she, her sister, al-Zubayr, and so-and-so and so-and-so had entered consecration for the lesser pilgrimage, and when they touched the Corner, they exited the state of consecration.

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (1641) and Muslim (1235). This is the wording of al-Bukhari.

٤٩٤٠ — عن محمد بن عبد الرحمن بن نوفل القرشي، أنه سأل عروة بن الزبير، فقال: قَدْ حَجَّ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ فَأَخْبَرَتْنِي عَائِشَةُ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا أَنَّهُ أَوَّلُ شَيْءٍ بَدَأَ بِهِ حِينَ قَدِمَ أَنَّهُ تَوَضَّأَ ثُمَّ طَافَ بِالْبَيْتِ، ثُمَّ لَمْ تَكُنْ عُمْرَةً، ثُمَّ حَجَّ أَبُو بَكْرٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ فَكَانَ أَوَّلَ شَيْءٍ بَدَأَ بِهِ الطَّوَافُ بِالْبَيْتِ، ثُمَّ لَمْ تَكُنْ عُمْرَةً، ثُمَّ عُمَرُ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ مِثْلُ ذَلِكَ، ثُمَّ حَجَّ عُثْمَانُ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ فَرَأَيْتُهُ أَوَّلَ شَيْءٍ بَدَأَ بِهِ الطَّوَافُ بِالْبَيْتِ، ثُمَّ لَمْ تَكُنْ عُمْرَةً، ثُمَّ مُعَاوِيَةُ وَعَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عُمَرَ، ثُمَّ حَجَجْتُ مَعَ أَبِي الزُّبَيْرِ بْنِ الْعَوَّامِ فَكَانَ أَوَّلَ شَيْءٍ بَدَأَ بِهِ الطَّوَافُ بِالْبَيْتِ، ثُمَّ لَمْ تَكُنْ عُمْرَةً، ثُمَّ رَأَيْتُ الْمُهَاجِرِينَ وَالْأَنْصَارَ يَفْعَلُونَ ذَلِكَ، ثُمَّ لَمْ تَكُنْ عُمْرَةً، ثُمَّ آخِرُ مَنْ رَأَيْتُ فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ ابْنُ عُمَرَ، ثُمَّ لَمْ يَنْقُضْهَا عُمْرَةً، وَهَذَا ابْنُ عُمَرَ عِنْدَهُمْ فَلَا يَسْأَلُونَهُ، وَلَا أَحَدٌ مِمَّنْ مَضَى مَا كَانُوا يَبْدَؤُونَ بِشَيْءٍ حَتَّى يَضَعُوا أَقْدَامَهُمْ مِنَ الطَّوَافِ بِالْبَيْتِ، ثُمَّ لَا يَحِلُّونَ، وَقَدْ رَأَيْتُ أُمِّي وَخَالَتِي حِينَ تَقْدَمَانِ لَا تَبْتَدِئَانِ بِشَيْءٍ أَوَّلَ مِنَ الْبَيْتِ تَطُوفَانِ بِهِ، ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمَا لَا تَحِلَّانِ، وَقَدْ أَخْبَرَتْنِي أُمِّي أَنَّهَا أَهَلَّتْ هِيَ وَأُخْتُهَا وَالزُّبَيْرُ وَفُلَانٌ وَفُلَانٌ بِعُمْرَةٍ، فَلَمَّا مَسَحُوا الرُّكْنَ حَلُّوا.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاريّ (١٦٤١)، ومسلم (١٢٣٥). وهذا لفظ البخاريّ.

4940 — Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Nawfal al-Qurashi reported that he asked ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, and he said: The Prophet ﷺ performed the pilgrimage, and ‘A’ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, informed me that the first thing he began with when he arrived was that he performed ablution, then circled the House, and that was not a lesser pilgrimage. Then Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, performed the pilgrimage, and the first thing he began with was circling the House, and that was not a lesser pilgrimage. Then ‘Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, did the same. Then ‘Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, performed the pilgrimage, and I saw that the first thing he began with was circling the House, and that was not a lesser pilgrimage. Then Mu‘awiyah and ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar did the same. Then I performed the pilgrimage with my father al-Zubayr ibn al-‘Awwam, and the first thing he began with was circling the House, and that was not a lesser pilgrimage. Then I saw the Emigrants and the Helpers doing that, and that was not a lesser pilgrimage. Then the last person I saw doing that was Ibn ‘Umar, and he did not turn it into a lesser pilgrimage. And here is Ibn ‘Umar among them, yet they do not ask him. No one from those who passed before would begin with anything before placing their feet in the circling of the House, then they would not exit the state of consecration. I also saw my mother and my aunt, when they arrived, not begin with anything before the House, circling it, and then they did not exit the state of consecration. My mother informed me that she, her sister, al-Zubayr, and so-and-so and so-and-so had entered consecration for the lesser pilgrimage, and when they touched the Corner, they exited the state of consecration.

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (1641) and Muslim (1235). This is the wording of al-Bukhari.

٤٩٤١ — عن أبي ذرٍّ قال: كانت المتعة في الحجِّ لأصحاب محمد ﷺ خاصّةً.

صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٢٢٤).

قوله: (( كانت المتعة في الحج )) أي فسخ الحج إلى العمرة، وإلا فأصل المتعة في كتاب الله.

قال الأثرم في “سنته”: وذكر لنا أحمد بن حنبل أن عبد الرحمن بن مهدي حدّثه عن سفيان، عن الأعمش، عن إبراهيم التيمي، عن أبيه، عن أبي ذرٍّ: (( كانت لنا خاصّةً )). فقال أحمد بن حنبل: رحم الله أبا ذر، هي في كتاب الله: ( فَمَنْ تَمَتَّعَ بِالْعُمْرَةِ إِلَى الْحَجِّ ) [سورة البقرة: ١٩٦]. انظر: “زاد المعاد” (٢/١٩٤).

english_source:
4941 — Abu Dharr said: The concession connected to combining the lesser pilgrimage with the pilgrimage was specifically for the Companions of Muhammad ﷺ.

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1224).

His statement, “the concession connected to the pilgrimage,” means changing the pilgrimage into the lesser pilgrimage. Otherwise, the basis of beginning with the lesser pilgrimage and then continuing to the pilgrimage is found in the Book of Allah.

Al-Athram said in his “Sunan”: Ahmad ibn Hanbal told us that ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to him from Sufyan, from al-A‘mash, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from his father, from Abu Dharr: “It was specifically for us.” Ahmad ibn Hanbal then said: “May Allah have mercy on Abu Dharr. It is in the Book of Allah: ‘Whoever enjoys the lesser pilgrimage until the pilgrimage…’” [Surat al-Baqarah: 196]. See “Zad al-Ma‘ad” (2/194).

٤٩٤٣ — عن أبي نضرة، قال: كَانَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ يَأْمُرُ بِالْمُتْعَةِ، وَكَانَ ابْنُ الزُّبَيْرِ يَنْهَى عَنْهَا. قَالَ: فَذَكَرْتُ ذَلِكَ لِجَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، فَقَالَ: عَلَى يَدَيَّ دَارَ الْحَدِيثُ، تَمَتَّعْنَا مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ، فَلَمَّا قَامَ عُمَرُ قَالَ: إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ يُحِلُّ لِرَسُولِهِ مَا شَاءَ بِمَا شَاءَ، وَإِنَّ الْقُرْآنَ قَدْ نَزَلَ مَنَازِلَهُ، فَأَتِمُّوا الْحَجَّ وَالْعُمْرَةَ لِلَّهِ كَمَا أَمَرَكُمُ اللَّهُ، وَأَبِتُّوا نِكَاحَ هَذِهِ النِّسَاءِ، فَلَنْ أُوتَى بِرَجُلٍ نَكَحَ امْرَأَةً إِلَى أَجَلٍ إِلَّا رَجَمْتُهُ بِالْحِجَارَةِ.

ورواه مسلم أيضاً (١٢٤٩) عن أبي نضرة، قال: كنت عند جابر بن عبد الله، فأتاه آتٍ فقال: إن ابن عباس وابن الزبير اختلفا في المتعتين، فقال جابر: فعلناهما مع رسول الله ﷺ، ثم نهانا عنهما عمر فلم نعد لهما.

وفي رواية عند الإمام أحمد (٣٦٩) قال جابر: تمتعنا مع رسول الله ﷺ ومع أبي بكر، فلما ولي عمر بن الخطاب خطب الناس فقال: إن القرآن هو القرآن، وإن رسول الله ﷺ هو الرسول، وإنهما كانتا متعتان على عهد رسول الله ﷺ: إحداهما متعة الحج، والأخرى متعة النساء.

صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٢١٧).

قوله: (( المتعتين )) أي متعة الحج ومتعة النساء.

قال شيخ الإسلام ابن تيمية رحمه الله: ومعلوم أن التمتع بالعمرة إلى الحج لا يكره بالاتفاق، فيجب حمل نهيهم على متعة الفسخ، ورخصة المتعة المبتدأة، توفيقًا بين أقاويلهم.

4943 — Abu Nadrah said: Ibn ‘Abbas used to command the temporary combining connected to pilgrimage, while Ibn al-Zubayr used to forbid it. He said: I mentioned that to Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, and he said: The discussion passed through my own hands. We did it with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then when ‘Umar took office, he said: “Allah used to permit for His Messenger whatever He willed in whatever way He willed, and the Qur’an has now taken its settled place, so complete the pilgrimage and the lesser pilgrimage for Allah as Allah commanded you, and make the marriages of these women definite and binding. If I am brought a man who married a woman for a fixed term, I will stone him.”

Muslim also narrated (1249) from Abu Nadrah, who said: I was with Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah when someone came to him and said: Ibn ‘Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr differed concerning the two temporary permissions. Jabir said: We did both of them with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then ‘Umar forbade us from them, so we did not return to them.

In a narration recorded by Imam Ahmad (369), Jabir said: We practiced this with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and with Abu Bakr. Then when ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab became leader, he addressed the people and said: “The Qur’an is the Qur’an, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is the Messenger, and there were two temporary permissions during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: one was the temporary combining in pilgrimage, and the other was temporary marriage.”

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1217).

٤٩٤٣ — عن أبي نضرة، قال: كَانَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ يَأْمُرُ بِالْمُتْعَةِ، وَكَانَ ابْنُ الزُّبَيْرِ يَنْهَى عَنْهَا. قَالَ: فَذَكَرْتُ ذَلِكَ لِجَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، فَقَالَ: عَلَى يَدَيَّ دَارَ الْحَدِيثُ، تَمَتَّعْنَا مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ، فَلَمَّا قَامَ عُمَرُ قَالَ: إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ يُحِلُّ لِرَسُولِهِ مَا شَاءَ بِمَا شَاءَ، وَإِنَّ الْقُرْآنَ قَدْ نَزَلَ مَنَازِلَهُ، فَأَتِمُّوا الْحَجَّ وَالْعُمْرَةَ لِلَّهِ كَمَا أَمَرَكُمُ اللَّهُ، وَأَبِتُّوا نِكَاحَ هَذِهِ النِّسَاءِ، فَلَنْ أُوتَى بِرَجُلٍ نَكَحَ امْرَأَةً إِلَى أَجَلٍ إِلَّا رَجَمْتُهُ بِالْحِجَارَةِ.

٤٩٤٤ — عن عروة بن الزبير: أنه أتى ابن عباس، فقال: يا ابن عباس، طالما أضللتَ الناس! قال: وما ذاك يا عُرَيَّةُ؟ قال: الرجل يخرج محرماً بحجٍّ أو عمرةٍ، فإذا طاف زعمتَ أنه قد حلَّ، فقد كان أبو بكر وعمر ينهيان عن ذلك. فقال: أَهُمَا - ويحكَ - آثَرُ عندك أم ما في كتاب الله وما سنَّ رسول الله ﷺ في أصحابه وفي أمته؟ فقال عروة: هما كانا أعلم بكتاب الله وما سنَّ رسول الله مني ومنك. قال ابن أبي مليكة: فخصمه عروة.

حسن: رواه الطبراني في الأوسط (٢١).

english_source:
4944 — ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr came to Ibn ‘Abbas and said: O Ibn ‘Abbas, how often you have led people astray! He said: What is that, O little ‘Urwah? He said: A man leaves in consecration for pilgrimage or lesser pilgrimage, then once he circles the House you claim that he has exited consecration, while Abu Bakr and ‘Umar used to forbid that. So he said: “Are those two — woe to you — more deserving to be followed in your view than what is in the Book of Allah and what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ established among his Companions and his community?” ‘Urwah said: Those two were more knowledgeable than me and you regarding the Book of Allah and what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ established. Ibn Abi Mulaykah said: ‘Urwah overcame him in the debate.

Hasan: Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Awsat (21).

٤٩٤٥ — عن أبي عمران أسلم، أنه قال: حججتُ مع موالي، فدخلتُ على أمِّ سلمة زوج النبيِّ ﷺ فقلتُ: أأعتمر قبل أن أحجَّ؟ قالت: إن شئتَ فاعتمر قبل أن تحجَّ، وإن شئتَ بعد أن تحجَّ. قال: فقلتُ: إنهم يقولون: من كان صَرُورةً فلا يصلح أن يعتمر قبل أن يحجَّ. قال: فسألتُ أمهات المؤمنين، فقلن مثل ما قالت، فرجعتُ إليها فأخبرتُها بقولهن، فقالت: نعم، وأنا أُشفيك، سمعتُ رسول الله ﷺ يقول: (( أَهِلُّوا يَا آلَ مُحَمَّدٍ بِعُمْرَةٍ فِي حَجٍّ )).

صحيح: رواه الإمام أحمد (٢٦٥٤٨)، والطبراني في الكبير (٢٣/٣٤١)، والبيهقيّ (٤/٣٥٥).

english_source:
4945 — Abu ‘Imran Aslam said: I performed the pilgrimage with my patrons, then I entered upon Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, and said: Should I perform the lesser pilgrimage before the pilgrimage? She said: If you wish, perform the lesser pilgrimage before the pilgrimage, and if you wish, after the pilgrimage. He said: I said: They say that whoever has never performed the pilgrimage before should not perform the lesser pilgrimage before the pilgrimage. He said: So I asked the Mothers of the Believers, and they said the same as she had said. Then I returned to her and informed her of what they had said. She said: Yes, and I will settle it for you fully: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say, “O family of Muhammad, enter consecration for a lesser pilgrimage within a pilgrimage.”

Authentic: Narrated by Imam Ahmad (26548), al-Tabarani in al-Kabir (23/341), and al-Bayhaqi (4/355).

٤٩٤٥ — عن أبي عمران أسلم، أنه قال: حججتُ مع موالي، فدخلتُ على أمِّ سلمة زوج النبيِّ ﷺ فقلتُ: أأعتمر قبل أن أحجَّ؟ قالت: إن شئتَ فاعتمر قبل أن تحجَّ، وإن شئتَ بعد أن تحجَّ. قال: فقلتُ: إنهم يقولون: من كان صَرُورةً فلا يصلح أن يعتمر قبل أن يحجَّ. قال: فسألتُ أمهات المؤمنين، فقلن مثل ما قالت، فرجعتُ إليها فأخبرتُها بقولهن، فقالت: نعم، وأنا أُشفيك، سمعتُ رسول الله ﷺ يقول: (( أَهِلُّوا يَا آلَ مُحَمَّدٍ بِعُمْرَةٍ فِي حَجٍّ )).

٤٩٤٦ — عن بكر، عن أنس، قال: سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ يُلَبِّي بِالْحَجِّ وَالْعُمْرَةِ جَمِيعًا. قال بكر: فحدّثتُ بذلك ابنَ عمر، فقال: لبَّى بالحجِّ وحده. فلقيتُ أنسًا فحدّثتُه بقول ابن عمر، فقال أنس: ما تعدُّوننا إلا صبيانًا! سمعتُ رسول الله ﷺ يقول: (( لَبَّيْكَ عُمْرَةً وَحَجًّا )).

٤٩٤٧ — عن أنس، قال: صَلَّى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ وَنَحْنُ مَعَهُ بِالْمَدِينَةِ الظُّهْرَ أَرْبَعًا، وَالْعَصْرَ بِذِي الْحُلَيْفَةِ رَكْعَتَيْنِ، ثُمَّ بَاتَ بِهَا حَتَّى أَصْبَحَ، ثُمَّ رَكِبَ حَتَّى اسْتَوَتْ بِهِ عَلَى الْبَيْدَاءِ، حَمِدَ اللَّهَ وَسَبَّحَ وَكَبَّرَ، ثُمَّ أَهَلَّ بِحَجٍّ وَعُمْرَةٍ، وَأَهَلَّ النَّاسُ بِهِمَا.

صحيح: رواه البخاريّ (١٥٥١) ومسلم (٦٩٠).

english_source:
4947 — Anas said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the noon prayer with us in Medina as four units, and the afternoon prayer at Dhu al-Hulayfah as two units. Then he stayed there overnight until morning. Then he mounted, and when his mount stood upright with him upon al-Bayda’, he praised Allah, glorified Him, and declared His greatness, then he proclaimed both a pilgrimage and a lesser pilgrimage, and the people proclaimed both with him.

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (1551) and Muslim (690).

٤٩٥٠ — عن سالم بن عبد الله أنه سمع رجلاً من أهل الشام، وهو يسأل عبد الله بن عمر عن التمتع بالعمرة إلى الحج؟ فقال عبد الله بن عمر: هي حلال. فقال الشامي: إن أباك قد نهى عنها؟ فقال عبد الله بن عمر: أرأيتَ إن كان أبي نهى عنها، وصنعها رسول الله ﷺ، أأمر أبي نتبع أم أمر رسول الله؟ فقال الرجل: بل أمر رسول الله ﷺ. فقال: لقد صنعها رسول الله ﷺ.

صحيح: رواه الترمذيّ (٨٢٤).

التمتع هنا بمعنى القران، أي أنه ﷺ أتى بعمل العمرة غير الحلق والتقصير، ثم حجَّ، وهو القِران، ثم صار التمتع في الاصطلاح: من أتى بنسكين في سفر واحد مستقلين.

english_source:
4950 — Salim ibn ‘Abd Allah said that he heard a man from the people of Syria asking ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar about beginning with the lesser pilgrimage and then continuing to the pilgrimage. ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar said: It is lawful. The Syrian man said: But your father forbade it. ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar said: Tell me — if my father forbade it, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did it, should the command of my father be followed or the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? The man said: Rather, the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ indeed did it.

Authentic: Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (824).

Here, this beginning form means combining both rites, meaning that he ﷺ performed the actions of the lesser pilgrimage except shaving or cutting the hair, then continued with the pilgrimage, and that is the combined form. Later, in juristic usage, the term came to mean performing two rites in one journey as two distinct acts.

٤٩٥٠ — عن سالم بن عبد الله أنه سمع رجلاً من أهل الشام، وهو يسأل عبد الله بن عمر عن التمتع بالعمرة إلى الحج؟ فقال عبد الله بن عمر: هي حلال. فقال الشامي: إن أباك قد نهى عنها؟ فقال عبد الله بن عمر: أرأيتَ إن كان أبي نهى عنها، وصنعها رسول الله ﷺ، أأمر أبي نتبع أم أمر رسول الله؟ فقال الرجل: بل أمر رسول الله ﷺ. فقال: لقد صنعها رسول الله ﷺ.

صحيح: رواه الترمذيّ (٨٢٤).

التمتع هنا بمعنى القران، أي أنه ﷺ أتى بعمل العمرة غير الحلق والتقصير، ثم حجَّ، وهو القِران، ثم صار التمتع في الاصطلاح: من أتى بنسكين في سفر واحد مستقلين.

4950 — Salim ibn ‘Abd Allah said that he heard a man from the people of Syria asking ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar about beginning with the lesser pilgrimage and then continuing to the pilgrimage. ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar said: It is lawful. The man said: Rather, the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ indeed did it.

Authentic: Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (824).

Here, this beginning form means combining both rites, meaning that he ﷺ performed the actions of the lesser pilgrimage except shaving or cutting the hair, then continued with the pilgrimage, and that is the combined form. Later, in juristic usage, the term came to mean performing two rites in one journey as two distinct acts.

٤٩٥١ — عن عائشة أنها قالت: خَرَجْنَا مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ عَامَ حَجَّةِ الْوَدَاعِ، فَمِنَّا مَنْ أَهَلَّ بِعُمْرَةٍ، وَمِنَّا مَنْ أَهَلَّ بِحَجَّةٍ وَعُمْرَةٍ، وَمِنَّا مَنْ أَهَلَّ بِالْحَجِّ، وَأَهَلَّ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ بِالْحَجِّ، فَأَمَّا مَنْ أَهَلَّ بِعُمْرَةٍ فَحَلَّ، وَأَمَّا مَنْ أَهَلَّ بِحَجٍّ أَوْ جَمَعَ الْحَجَّ وَالْعُمْرَةَ فَلَمْ يَحِلُّوا حَتَّى كَانَ يَوْمُ النَّحْرِ.

متفق عليه: رواه مالك (٣٦) والبخاريّ (١٥٦٢)، ومسلم (١١٨:١٢١١).

english_source:
4951 — ‘A’ishah said: We set out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage. Some of us entered consecration for the lesser pilgrimage, some for both the pilgrimage and the lesser pilgrimage, and some for the pilgrimage alone. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered consecration for the pilgrimage. As for those who entered consecration for the lesser pilgrimage, they exited consecration; and as for those who entered consecration for the pilgrimage, or combined the pilgrimage and the lesser pilgrimage, they did not exit consecration until the Day of Sacrifice.

Agreed upon: Narrated by Malik (36), al-Bukhari (1562), and Muslim (1211:118).

٤٩٥٢ — عن بكر - وهو ابن عبد الله المزني - أنه ذكر لابن عمر أن أنسًا حدَّثهم أن النبيَّ ﷺ أهلَّ بعمرةٍ وحجّةٍ. فقال: أهلَّ النبيُّ ﷺ بالحجِّ، وأهللنا به معه، فلمَّا قدمنا مكة قال: (( مَنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ مَعَهُ هَدْيٌ فَلْيَجْعَلْهَا عُمْرَةً )). وكان مع النبيِّ ﷺ هَدْيٌ، فقدم علينا عليُّ بن أبي طالب من اليمن حاجًّا، فقال النبيُّ ﷺ: (( بِمَ أَهْلَلْتَ؟ فَإِنَّ مَعَنَا هَدْيًا )). قال: أهللتُ بما أهلَّ به النبيُّ ﷺ. قال: (( فَأَمْسِكْ، فَإِنَّ مَعَنَا هَدْيًا )).

صحيح: رواه البخاريّ (٤٣٥٤، ٤٣٥٣) ومسلم (١٢٣٢).

4952 — Bakr — who is Ibn ‘Abd Allah al-Muzani — mentioned to Ibn ‘Umar that Anas had told them that the Prophet ﷺ entered consecration for a lesser pilgrimage and a pilgrimage. Ibn ‘Umar said: The Prophet ﷺ entered consecration for the pilgrimage, and we entered consecration for it with him. When we arrived in Mecca, he said: “Whoever among you does not have a sacrificial animal with him should make it a lesser pilgrimage.” The Prophet ﷺ had sacrificial animals with him. Then ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib came to us from Yemen as a pilgrim, and the Prophet ﷺ said: “For what did you enter consecration? For we have sacrificial animals with us.” He said: I entered consecration for what the Prophet ﷺ entered consecration for. He said: “Then remain in consecration, for we have sacrificial animals with us.”

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (4354, 4353) and Muslim (1232).

4954 — Al-Subayyi‘ ibn Ma‘bad said: I was a desert Arab and a Christian, then I accepted Islam. I came to a man from my clan named Hudaym ibn Qarmalah and said to him: O my good man, I am eager for striving in the path of Allah, and I have found that the pilgrimage and the lesser pilgrimage are both prescribed upon me, so how can I combine them? He said: Combine them, and slaughter whatever sacrificial animal is easy for you. So I entered consecration for both together. When I came to al-‘Udhayb, Salman ibn Rabi‘ah and Zayd ibn Suhan met me while I was entering consecration for both together, and one of them said to the other: This man is no more knowledgeable than his camel. He said: It was as if a mountain had been cast upon me, until I came to ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab and said to him: O Commander of the Believers, I was a desert Arab and a Christian, then I accepted Islam while eager for striving in the path of Allah, and I found that the pilgrimage and the lesser pilgrimage are both prescribed upon me, so I came to a man from my people and he said to me: Combine them and slaughter whatever sacrificial animal is easy for you. So I entered consecration for both together. Then ‘Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said to me: “You have been guided to the Sunnah of your Prophet ﷺ.”

Authentic: Narrated by Abu Dawud (1799) — this is his wording — al-Nasa’i (2719), and Ibn Hibban (3970).

٤٩٥٥ — عن عبد الله بن عمر، أنه قال حين خرج إلى مكة معتمرًا في الفتنة: إِنْ صُدِدْتُ عَنِ الْبَيْتِ صَنَعْنَا كَمَا صَنَعْنَا مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ، فَأَهَلَّ بِعُمْرَةٍ مِنْ أَجْلِ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ أَهَلَّ بِعُمْرَةٍ عَامَ الْحُدَيْبِيَةِ، ثُمَّ إِنَّ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ نَظَرَ فِي أَمْرِهِ فَقَالَ: مَا أَمْرُهُمَا إِلَّا وَاحِدٌ، ثُمَّ الْتَفَتَ إِلَى أَصْحَابِهِ فَقَالَ: مَا أَمْرُهُمَا إِلَّا وَاحِدٌ، أُشْهِدُكُمْ أَنِّي قَدْ أَوْجَبْتُ الْحَجَّ مَعَ الْعُمْرَةِ، ثُمَّ نَفَذَ حَتَّى جَاءَ الْبَيْتَ فَطَافَ طَوَافًا وَاحِدًا وَرَأَى ذَلِكَ مُجْزِئًا عَنْهُ وَأَهْدَى.

متفق عليه: رواه مالك (٩٩) والبخاريّ (١٨١٣)، ومسلم (١٢٣٠) إلا أن مسلمًا قال: (( فخرج حتى إذا جاء البيت طاف به سبعًا وبين الصفا والمروة سبعًا لم يزد عليه… )).

ورواه البخاريّ (١٦٩٣)، ومسلم (١٨٣:١٢٣٠).

متفق عليه: رواه مالك (٩٩) والبخاريّ (١٨١٣)، ومسلم (١٢٣٠) إلا أن مسلمًا قال: (( فخرج حتى إذا جاء البيت طاف به سبعًا وبين الصفا والمروة سبعًا لم يزد عليه… )).

4955 — ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar said, when he set out to Mecca for the lesser pilgrimage during the time of unrest: “If I am prevented from reaching the House, we will do as we did with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.” So he entered consecration for a lesser pilgrimage because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had entered consecration for a lesser pilgrimage in the year of al-Hudaybiyah. Then ‘Abd Allah reconsidered the matter and said: “The ruling of the two is only one.” Then he turned to his companions and said: “The ruling of the two is only one. I call you to witness that I have now joined the pilgrimage with the lesser pilgrimage.” Then he went on until he came to the House, and he performed one circumambulation, and considered that sufficient for him, and he offered a sacrificial animal.

Agreed upon: Narrated by Malik (99), al-Bukhari (1813), and Muslim (1230), except that Muslim said: “He went on until he came to the House, then circumambulated it seven times and went between al-Safa and al-Marwah seven times, and did not add more than that…”

It was also narrated by al-Bukhari (1693) and Muslim (1230:183).

٤٩٥٦ — عن عائشة، قالت: خَرَجْنَا مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ عَامَ حَجَّةِ الْوَدَاعِ فَأَهْلَلْنَا بِعُمْرَةٍ، ثُمَّ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: (( مَنْ كَانَ مَعَهُ هَدْيٌ فَلْيُهِلَّ بِالْحَجِّ مَعَ الْعُمْرَةِ، ثُمَّ لَا يَحِلُّ حَتَّى يَحِلَّ مِنْهُمَا جَمِيعًا )). قالت: فَقَدِمْتُ مَكَّةَ وَأَنَا حَائِضٌ فَلَمْ أَطُفْ بِالْبَيْتِ وَلَا بَيْنَ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ، فَشَكَوْتُ ذَلِكَ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ فَقَالَ: (( انْقُضِي رَأْسَكِ وَامْتَشِطِي وَأَهِلِّي بِالْحَجِّ وَدَعِي الْعُمْرَةَ )). قالت: فَفَعَلْتُ، فَلَمَّا قَضَيْنَا الْحَجَّ أَرْسَلَنِي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ مَعَ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي بَكْرٍ الصِّدِّيقِ إِلَى التَّنْعِيمِ فَاعْتَمَرْتُ، فَقَالَ: (( هَذَا مَكَانُ عُمْرَتِكِ )).

فَطَافَ الَّذِينَ أَهَلُّوا بِالْعُمْرَةِ بِالْبَيْتِ وَبَيْنَ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ، ثُمَّ حَلُّوا مِنْهَا، ثُمَّ طَافُوا طَوَافًا آخَرَ بَعْدَ أَنْ رَجَعُوا مِنْ مِنًى لِحَجِّهِمْ. وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ كَانُوا أَهَلُّوا بِالْحَجِّ أَوْ جَمَعُوا الْحَجَّ وَالْعُمْرَةَ فَإِنَّمَا طَافُوا طَوَافًا وَاحِدًا.

متفق عليه: رواه مالك (٢٢٣) والبخاريّ (١٥٥٦)، ومسلم (١١١:١٢١١).

english_source:
4956 — ‘A’ishah said: We set out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage and entered consecration for the lesser pilgrimage. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever has a sacrificial animal with him should enter consecration for the pilgrimage together with the lesser pilgrimage, then he should not come out of consecration until he comes out of both together.” She said: I arrived in Mecca while menstruating, so I did not circumambulate the House nor go between al-Safa and al-Marwah. I complained about that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: “Undo your hair, comb it, enter consecration for the pilgrimage, and leave the lesser pilgrimage.” She said: So I did that. Then when we completed the pilgrimage, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me with ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq to al-Tan‘im, and I performed the lesser pilgrimage. He then said: “This is in place of your lesser pilgrimage.”

Those who had entered consecration for the lesser pilgrimage circumambulated the House and went between al-Safa and al-Marwah, then came out of consecration. Then they performed another circumambulation after returning from Mina for their pilgrimage. As for those who had entered consecration for the pilgrimage, or had combined the pilgrimage and the lesser pilgrimage, they only performed one circumambulation.

Agreed upon: Narrated by Malik (223), al-Bukhari (1556), and Muslim (1211:111).

٤٩٥٦ — عن عائشة، قالت: خَرَجْنَا مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ عَامَ حَجَّةِ الْوَدَاعِ فَأَهْلَلْنَا بِعُمْرَةٍ، ثُمَّ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: (( مَنْ كَانَ مَعَهُ هَدْيٌ فَلْيُهِلَّ بِالْحَجِّ مَعَ الْعُمْرَةِ، ثُمَّ لَا يَحِلُّ حَتَّى يَحِلَّ مِنْهُمَا جَمِيعًا )). قالت: فَقَدِمْتُ مَكَّةَ وَأَنَا حَائِضٌ فَلَمْ أَطُفْ بِالْبَيْتِ وَلَا بَيْنَ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ، فَشَكَوْتُ ذَلِكَ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ فَقَالَ: (( انْقُضِي رَأْسَكِ وَامْتَشِطِي وَأَهِلِّي بِالْحَجِّ وَدَعِي الْعُمْرَةَ )). قالت: فَفَعَلْتُ، فَلَمَّا قَضَيْنَا الْحَجَّ أَرْسَلَنِي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ مَعَ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي بَكْرٍ الصِّدِّيقِ إِلَى التَّنْعِيمِ فَاعْتَمَرْتُ، فَقَالَ: (( هَذَا مَكَانُ عُمْرَتِكِ )).

فَطَافَ الَّذِينَ أَهَلُّوا بِالْعُمْرَةِ بِالْبَيْتِ وَبَيْنَ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ، ثُمَّ حَلُّوا مِنْهَا، ثُمَّ طَافُوا طَوَافًا آخَرَ بَعْدَ أَنْ رَجَعُوا مِنْ مِنًى لِحَجِّهِمْ. وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ كَانُوا أَهَلُّوا بِالْحَجِّ أَوْ جَمَعُوا الْحَجَّ وَالْعُمْرَةَ فَإِنَّمَا طَافُوا طَوَافًا وَاحِدًا.

متفق عليه: رواه مالك (٢٢٣) والبخاريّ (١٥٥٦)، ومسلم (١١١:١٢١١).

4956 — ‘A’ishah said: We set out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage and entered consecration for the lesser pilgrimage. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever has a sacrificial animal with him should enter consecration for the pilgrimage together with the lesser pilgrimage, then he should not come out of consecration until he comes out of both together.” She said: I arrived in Mecca while menstruating, so I did not circumambulate the House nor go between al-Safa and al-Marwah. I complained about that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: “Undo your hair, comb it, enter consecration for the pilgrimage, and leave the lesser pilgrimage.” She said: So I did that. Then when we completed the pilgrimage, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me with ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq to al-Tan‘im, and I performed the lesser pilgrimage. He then said: “This is in place of your lesser pilgrimage.”

Those who had entered consecration for the lesser pilgrimage circumambulated the House and went between al-Safa and al-Marwah, then came out of consecration. Then they performed another circumambulation after returning from Mina for their pilgrimage. As for those who had entered consecration for the pilgrimage, or had combined the pilgrimage and the lesser pilgrimage, they only performed one circumambulation.

Agreed upon: Narrated by Malik (223), al-Bukhari (1556), and Muslim (1211:111).

4958 — Abu Hurayrah said: Abu Bakr sent me during that pilgrimage among callers whom he sent on the Day of Sacrifice, announcing in Mina: “After this year, no idolater shall perform pilgrimage, and no one shall circumambulate the House naked.”

Humayd ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib after him and commanded him to proclaim Surat Bara’ah.

Abu Hurayrah said: ‘Ali proclaimed with us on the Day of Sacrifice among the people of Mina the message of Bara’ah, and that after this year no idolater should perform pilgrimage and no one should circumambulate the House naked.

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (4655).

arabic_source:
٤٩٥٩ — عن ابن عباس، قال: كَانَتِ الْمَرْأَةُ تَطُوفُ بِالْبَيْتِ وَهِيَ عُرْيَانَةٌ، فَتَقُولُ: مَنْ يُعِيرُنِي تِطْوَافًا، تَجْعَلُهُ عَلَى فَرْجِهَا، وَتَقُولُ:

الْيَوْمَ يَبْدُو بَعْضُهُ أَوْ كُلُّهُ

فَمَا بَدَا مِنْهُ فَلَا أُحِلُّهُ

فَنَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ الْآيَةُ: ( خُذُوا زِينَتَكُمْ عِنْدَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٍ ) [سورة الأعراف: ٣١].

صحيح: رواه مسلم في التفسير (٣٠٢٨).

وقوله: (( تِطْوَافًا )) هو ثوب تلبسه المرأة تطوف به.

ابتدعت قريش - قبل حادثة الفيل أو بعدها - ألَّا يطوف بالبيت أحد من غيرهم إلا بثياب أحدهم، فإن لم يجد طاف عريانًا، فإن خالف وطاف بثيابه ألقاها إذا فرغ، ولا يأخذها أبدًا، وتُداس بالأرجل، فجاء الإسلام بهدم هذه العادة الجاهلية.

وقوله: (( تقول … إلخ )) أي تطوف عريانة وتنشد هذا الشعر، وحاصله: اليوم يظهر بعض الفرج أو كله، وعلى التقديرين فلا أُبيح لأحد أن ينظر إليه قصدًا. تريد أنها كشفت الفرج لضرورة الطواف، لا لإباحة النظر إليه والاستمتاع به، فليس لأحد أن يفعل ذلك. قاله السيوطي في شرح النسائي.

فجاء الإسلام وأمر الله بستر العورة، فقال تعالى: ( يَا بَنِي آدَمَ خُذُوا زِينَتَكُمْ عِنْدَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٍ )، وقال النبي ﷺ: (( لا يطوف بالبيت عريان )).

٤٩٦٠ — عن أبي هريرة، قال: أَقْبَلَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ فَدَخَلَ مَكَّةَ، فَأَقْبَلَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ إِلَى الْحَجَرِ فَاسْتَلَمَهُ، ثُمَّ طَافَ بِالْبَيْتِ، ثُمَّ أَتَى الصَّفَا فَعَلَاهُ حَيْثُ يَنْظُرُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ، فَرَفَعَ يَدَيْهِ، فَجَعَلَ يَذْكُرُ اللَّهَ مَا شَاءَ أَنْ يَذْكُرَهُ وَيَدْعُوهُ. قَالَ: وَالْأَنْصَارُ تَحْتَهُ. قَالَ هَاشِمٌ: فَدَعَا وَحَمِدَ اللَّهَ وَدَعَا بِمَا شَاءَ أَنْ يَدْعُوَ.

صحيح: رواه أبو داود (١٨٧٢)، والإمام أحمد (١٠٩٤٨).

ورواه أبو داود (١٨٧١) أيضًا وزاد فيه: (( وصلَّى ركعتين خلف المقام )) بعد قوله: (( لما دخل مكة طاف بالبيت )).

4960 — Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and entered Mecca. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went to the Black Stone and touched it, then circumambulated the House. Then he came to al-Safa and climbed it where he could look toward the House. Then he raised his hands and began remembering Allah as much as he wished and supplicating to Him. He said: The Helpers were below him. Hashim said: Then he supplicated, praised Allah, and supplicated with whatever he wished to supplicate.

Authentic: Narrated by Abu Dawud (1872) and Imam Ahmad (10948).

Abu Dawud (1871) also narrated it with the addition: “And he prayed two units behind the Station,” after the words: “When he entered Mecca, he circumambulated the House.”

4961 — Ibn ‘Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The Black Stone came down from Paradise, and it was whiter than milk, but the sins of the children of Adam made it black.”

Authentic: Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (877), who said: “Hasan Sahih,” and by al-Nasa’i (2935) and Ahmad (2795).

4962 — ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amr ibn al-‘As said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The Corner and the Station are two rubies from the rubies of Paradise. Allah erased their light, and had He not done so, they would have illuminated everything between the east and the west.”

Hasan: Narrated by Ibn Khuzaymah (2731), al-Hakim (1/456), and al-Bayhaqi (5/75).

Authentic: Narrated by Imam Ahmad (5621), Ibn Hibban (3698), and ‘Abd al-Razzaq in his Musannaf (8877).

٤٩٦٤ — عن المنكدر بن عبد الله قال: قال رسول اللّه ﷺ: (( مَنْ طَافَ حَوْلَ الْبَيْتِ أُسْبُوعًا لَا يَلْغُو فِيهِ كَانَ كَعَدْلِ رَقَبَةٍ يَعْتِقُهَا )).

4964 — Al-Munkadir ibn ‘Abd Allah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever circumambulates the House seven times, not engaging in vain talk during it, will have the reward equal to freeing a slave.”

Hasan: Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Kabir (20/360), and from him Abu Nu‘aym in “Ma‘rifat al-Sahabah” (5/2601).

٤٩٦٥ — عن عبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير، أنَّ رجلًا قال: يا أبا عبد الرحمن، ما أراك تستلم إلا هذين الركنين؟ قال: إنِّي سمعتُ رسولَ اللّٰه ﷺ يقول: (( إِنَّ مَسْحَهُمَا يَحُطَّانِ الْخَطِيئَةَ )).

وسمعتُه يقول: (( مَنْ طَافَ سَبْعًا فَهُوَ كَعِدْلِ رَقَبَةٍ )).

صحيح: رواه النسائيّ (٢٩١٩).

4965 — ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Ubayd ibn ‘Umayr narrated that a man said: O Abu ‘Abd al-Rahman, I see you touching only these two corners. He replied: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Touching them removes sins.”

And I heard him say: “Whoever circumambulates seven times, it is like freeing a slave.”

Authentic: Narrated by al-Nasa’i (2919).

4966 — Ibn ‘Umar said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever circumambulates this House seven times and completes it carefully, it is like freeing a slave.”

And I heard him say: “He does not place one foot down nor raise the other except that Allah removes a sin from him and writes for him a good deed because of it.”

Authentic: Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (959), al-Hakim (1/489), and Ibn Hibban (3697).

٤٩٦٨ — عن عمر بن الخطاب، قال للركن: أَمَا وَاللَّهِ إِنِّي لَأَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ حَجَرٌ لَا تَضُرُّ وَلَا تَنْفَعُ، وَلَوْلَا أَنِّي رَأَيْتُ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ اسْتَلَمَكَ مَا اسْتَلَمْتُكَ. فَاسْتَلَمَهُ، ثُمَّ قَالَ: فَمَا لَنَا وَلِلرَّمَلِ؟ إِنَّمَا كُنَّا رَاءَيْنَا بِهِ الْمُشْرِكِينَ وَقَدْ أَهْلَكَهُمُ اللَّهُ. ثُمَّ قَالَ: شَيْءٌ صَنَعَهُ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ فَلَا نُحِبُّ أَنْ نَتْرُكَهُ.

صحيح: رواه البخاريّ (١٦٠٥).

english_source:
4968 — ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab said to the Corner: “By Allah, I certainly know that you are only a stone. You neither harm nor benefit. Had I not seen the Prophet ﷺ touch you, I would not have touched you.” Then he touched it and said: “What concern do we have with brisk walking? We only used to do it to show strength before the idolaters, and Allah has destroyed them.” Then he said: “It is something the Prophet ﷺ did, and we do not like to leave it.”

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (1605).

٤٩٧٠ — عن الزبير بن عربيّ قال: سأل رجلٌ ابنَ عمر رضي الله عنهما عن استلام الحجر؟ فقال: رأيتُ رسولَ اللّٰه ﷺ يستلمه ويقبّله. قال: قلتُ: أرأيتَ إن زُحِمتُ، أرأيتَ إن غُلِبتُ؟ قال: اجعلْ أَرَأَيْتَ باليمن! رأيتُ رسولَ اللّٰه ﷺ يستلمه ويقبّله.

صحيح: رواه البخاريّ (١٦١١).

4970 — Al-Zubayr ibn ‘Arabi said: A man asked Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, about touching the Stone. He said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ touch it and kiss it. The man said: What if I am crowded out? What if I am overpowered? He said: Leave your “what if” in Yemen. I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ touch it and kiss it.

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (1611).

٤٩٧٢ — عن عبيد بن جريج أنه قال لعبد الله بن عمر: يا أبا عبد الرحمن، رأيتُك تصنع أربعًا لم أرَ أحدًا من أصحابك يصنعها! قال: وما هنَّ يا ابن جريج؟ قال: رأيتُك لا تمسُّ من الأركان إلا اليمانيين، ورأيتُك تلبس النعال السِّبتية، ورأيتُك تصبغ بالصُّفرة، ورأيتُك إذا كنتَ بمكة أهلَّ الناسُ إذا رأوا الهلال ولم تُهِلَّ أنت حتى يكون يوم التروية؟ فقال عبد الله بن عمر: أمّا الأركان فإني لم أرَ رسول الله ﷺ يمسُّ إلا اليمانيين، وأمّا النعال السِّبتية فإني رأيتُ رسول الله ﷺ يلبس النعال التي ليس فيها شعر ويتوضأ فيها، فأنا أحب أن ألبسها، وأمّا الصُّفرة فإني رأيتُ رسول الله ﷺ يصبغ بها فأنا أحب أن أصبغ بها، وأمّا الإهلال فإني لم أرَ رسول الله ﷺ يُهِلُّ حتى تنبعث به راحلته.

متفق عليه: رواه مالك (٣١) والبخاريّ (١٦٦)، ومسلم (١١٨٧).

قوله: (( إلا اليمانيين )) قال النوويّ في شرح مسلم (٩٣/٨): (( والمراد بالركنين اليمانيين: الركن اليماني والركن الذي فيه الحجر الأسود… ويقال لهما اليمانيان تغليبًا لأحد الاسمين… فاليمانيان باقيان على قواعد إبراهيم بخلاف الشاميين؛ فلهذا لم يُستَلَما واستُلِم اليمانيان… قال القاضي عياض: وقد اتفق أئمة الأمصار والفقهاء اليوم على أن الركنين الشاميين لا يُستلمان، وإنما كان الخلاف في ذلك العصر الأول من بعض الصحابة وبعض التابعين، ثم ذهب )).

صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٢٦٩).

4976 — ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abbas said: I did not see the Messenger of Allah ﷺ touch any corners other than the two Yemeni corners.

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1269).

٤٩٧٧ — عن أبي الطفيل، قال: كنتُ مع ابن عباس، ومعاويةُ لا يمرّ بركنٍ إلا استلمه، فقال له ابنُ عباس: إنّ النبيَّ ﷺ لم يكن يستلم إلا الحجر الأسود، والركن اليماني.

فقال معاوية: ليس شيءٌ من البيت مهجورًا.

صحيح: رواه الترمذيّ (٨٥٨)، والإمام أحمد (٣٠٧٤)، وعبد الرزاق في مصنفه (٨٩٤٤).

4977 — Abu al-Tufayl said: I was with Ibn ‘Abbas, and Mu‘awiyah would not pass by any corner without touching it. So Ibn ‘Abbas said to him: The Prophet ﷺ only used to touch the Black Stone and the Yemeni Corner.

Mu‘awiyah replied: No part of the House is to be neglected.

Authentic: Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (858), Imam Ahmad (3074), and ‘Abd al-Razzaq in his Musannaf (8944).

٤٩٧٨ — عن عائشة، أنّ النبيّ ﷺ قال: (( أَلَمْ تَرَيْ أَنَّ قَوْمَكِ حِينَ بَنَوْا الْكَعْبَةَ اقْتَصَرُوا عَنْ قَوَاعِدِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ؟ )) قالت: فقلتُ: يا رسولَ اللّٰه، أفلا تردّها على قواعد إبراهيم؟ فقال رسولُ اللّٰه ﷺ: (( لولا حِدْثَانُ قومِكِ بالكفر لفعلتُ )).

قال: فقال عبدُ اللّٰه بنُ عمر: لئن كانت عائشةُ سمعتْ هذا من رسولِ اللّٰه ﷺ، ما أرى رسولَ اللّٰه ﷺ ترك استلام الركنين اللذين يليان الحِجر إلا أن البيت لم يُتمَّمْ على قواعد إبراهيم.

متفق عليه: رواه مالك (١٠٩)، والبخاريّ (١٥٨٣)، ومسلم (١٣٣٣:٣٩٩).

والحِجر - بكسر الجيم - هو الموضع المسمّى بالحطيم.

english_source:
4978 — ‘A’ishah reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Do you not see that your people, when they built the Ka‘bah, fell short of the foundations of Abraham?” She said: I said: O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, will you not return it to the foundations of Abraham? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Were it not for the fact that your people have only recently left disbelief, I would have done so.”

Then ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar said: If ‘A’ishah heard this from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then I do not think the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left touching the two corners next to the enclosure except because the House was not completed upon the foundations of Abraham.

Agreed upon: Narrated by Malik (109), al-Bukhari (1583), and Muslim (1333:399).

The enclosure, with the letter pronounced with a kasrah, is the place known as al-Hatim.

٤٩٧٩ — عن ابن عمر، أنه أُخبر بقول عائشة رضي اللّٰه عنها: إنّ الحِجر بعضه من البيت. فقال ابن عمر: واللهِ إنِّي لأظنُّ عائشةَ إن كانت سمعتْ هذا من رسولِ اللّٰه ﷺ، إنِّي لأظنّ رسولَ اللّٰه ﷺ لم يترك استلامهما إلا أنهما ليسا على قواعد البيت، ولا طاف الناس وراء الحِجر إلا لذلك.

صحيح: رواه أبو داود (١٨٧٥).

4979 — Ibn ‘Umar was informed of the statement of ‘A’ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that the enclosure is part of the House. Ibn ‘Umar said: By Allah, if ‘A’ishah indeed heard this from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then I believe the Messenger of Allah ﷺ only left touching those two corners because they are not upon the foundations of the House, and the people only circumambulate outside the enclosure because of that.

Authentic: Narrated by Abu Dawud (1875).

٤٩٨٢ — عن يعلى قال: طُفتُ مع عمر بن الخطاب، فلما كنتُ عند الركن الذي يلي الباب مما يلي الحِجر، أخذتُ بيده ليستلمه، فقال: أما طفتَ مع رسولِ اللّٰه ﷺ؟ قلت: بلى. قال: فهل رأيتَه يستلمه؟ قلت: لا. قال: فانفذْ عنك، فإنّ لك في رسولِ اللّٰه ﷺ أسوةً حسنةً.

صحيح: رواه الإمام أحمد (٢٥٣)، وأبو يعلى (١٨٢).

٤٩٨٣ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن السائب، قال: سمعتُ رسولَ اللّٰه ﷺ يقول ما بين الركنين: ( رَبَّنَا آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ ) [سورة البقرة: ٢٠١].

حسن: رواه أبو داود (١٨٩٢)، وصحّحه ابن خزيمة (٢٧٢١)، والحاكم (١/٤٥٥).

4983 — ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Sa’ib said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say between the two corners: “Our Lord, grant us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.” [Surat al-Baqarah: 201]

Hasan: Narrated by Abu Dawud (1892), authenticated by Ibn Khuzaymah (2721), and al-Hakim (1/455).

٤٩٨٤ — عن ابن عباس، قال: قال رسولُ اللّٰه ﷺ في الحجر: (( وَاللّٰهِ لَيَبْعَثَنَّهُ اللَّهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ، لَهُ عَيْنَانِ يُبْصِرُ بِهِمَا، وَلِسَانٌ يَنْطِقُ بِهِ، يَشْهَدُ عَلَى مَنِ اسْتَلَمَهُ بِحَقٍّ )).

حسن: رواه الترمذيّ (٩٦١)، وابن ماجه (٢٩٤٤)، وأحمد (٢٦٤٣، ٢٣٩٨، ٢٢١٥)، وصحّحه ابن خزيمة (٢٧٣٥).

english_source:
4984 — Ibn ‘Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said concerning the Stone: “By Allah, Allah will surely raise it on the Day of Resurrection, and it will have two eyes by which it sees and a tongue by which it speaks, testifying in favor of the one who touched it with truth.”

Hasan: Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (961), Ibn Majah (2944), Ahmad (2643, 2398, 2215), and authenticated by Ibn Khuzaymah (2735).

٤٩٨٥ — عن جعفر بن عبد اللّٰه بن عثمان، قال: رأيتُ محمدَ بنَ عبادِ بنِ جعفرٍ يستلم الحجر ثم يُقبِّلُه ويسجدُ عليه، فقلتُ له: ما هذا؟ فقال: رأيتُ خالكَ عبدَ اللّٰه بن عباسٍ يفعله. ثم قال: رأيتُ عمرَ فعله. ثم قال: إنِّي لأعلمُ أنّكَ حجرٌ، ولكنِّي رأيتُ رسولَ اللّٰه ﷺ يفعل هذا.

حسن: رواه الدارميّ (١٩٠٧)، وابن خزيمة (٢٧١٤)، والبزار - كشف الأستار (١١١٤).
